units.name: Jarmen Kell

tier.basis: Trained at the GLA Barracks once the player owns a Palace: his 1.04 Object file lists both buildings as prerequisites, and the wiki infobox and CNCNZ name the Palace. The Palace is the GLA's single tech building, which the tier map puts at t3, and the base-game manual tags him as a unit that building unlocks. All three GLA generals field him behind their own Barracks and Palace at the same price, so no GLA general lacks him: the Toxin and Stealth Generals' copies match the main one, and the Zero Hour manual lets the Toxin and Demolition Generals keep his camouflage although they give up other stealth. Only the Demolition General's copy adds buttons, a timed and a remote demolition charge for enemy buildings and a detonator (wiki, 1.04 command sets), left out because this entry follows the main GLA version (see uncertain). Each player may have one Kell alive at a time (MaxSimultaneousOfType in his Object file; the wiki, CNCNZ and the Zero Hour Academy tip say the same), and a new one can be trained once he dies. A player who has captured another GLA general's buildings can also train that general's Kell (wiki).

cost_band.basis: His list price, the same in the wiki infobox, on CNCNZ, as the build cost in his 1.04 Object file and for every GLA general's version, sits exactly on the very-high threshold, so it takes that band, since a value on an edge takes the higher band; it is about twice the mean price of the three anchor tanks.

mobility.notes: His land speed in the wiki infobox is half again the Ranger's and the Rebel's (his own locomotor in the 1.04 files agrees), a ratio exactly on the edge between medium and fast, which goes to medium; the wiki calls him quick for a foot soldier. Like most units he slows down when badly hurt, here to the Ranger's normal pace, a game-wide rule the band leaves out. His locomotor moves only on open ground and rubble, with no cliff surface, so unlike Colonel Burton he gets no climb trait; a Combat Cycle carries him over ground he could not cross on foot (wiki).

armour.notes: Step 1 of the armour-class steps decided: his set is Human Armor (his 1.04 Object file; the wiki infobox names it and lists its values), the set the Ranger, Pathfinder and Rebel also wear, which the armour_map makes unarmoured; the soldier rule keeps him there, since the set is no tougher than the basic rifleman's. He has only a little more health than a Ranger. The set takes double damage from sniper fire and from crushing, half again from flame and particle beams, half from lasers and only a tenth from tank shells and infantry missiles; only the Overlord and the Emperor can run him over (see strengths). One health bar; the self-healing of Elite and Heroic ranks belongs to veterancy and is left off. No armour upgrade reaches the main version: the wiki's Chemical Suits are for the Boss General's copy only.

sensors.notes: His fog-clearing figure, the second sight figure in the wiki infobox and the one the registry uses, equals the Ranger's, so the band is medium. His first figure, how far he picks targets, clears no fog and is twice the Ranger's; the wiki's praise of his sight fits that one. He could detect stealthed units until Zero Hour patch 1.03 took that away (wiki changelog), and his 1.04 Object file gives him no detector, so he has no sensor trait and can walk into mines, demo traps and hidden enemies (wiki). His own stealth is the cloak passive (abilities/1), as the registry's Generals stealth note asks, not the stealth sensor trait.

armament.name: Sniper rifle
armament.summary: His attack-button weapon, a scoped rifle: single shots at a quick, steady pace that land the instant he fires (game data) and reach a little over twice as far as the Ranger's rifle, well inside his own fog-clearing sight. Its Sniper damage (wiki infobox) counts double against the armour every ordinary soldier wears, so each hit drops a basic rifleman. Vehicles, aircraft and nearly every building take nothing from it, which also stops him aiming at them: the Fire Base, which takes sniper fire in full, is the one building it hurts, along with the troops inside, and at a Stinger Site it picks off the soldiers who man it. Soldiers garrisoned in a civilian building are out of its reach. AP Bullets, bought once at the Black Market for several GLA units, makes it hit a quarter harder. Firing it shows him to the enemy until a couple of seconds after he stops (abilities/1).

crew.notes: One soldier; one player is Kell. He takes one seat in a transport and garrisons civilian buildings like other infantry (game-wide), staying unseen inside, though he cannot snipe crews from there. He can ride a Combat Cycle, which then fires his rifle and his snipe and hides as he does (recorded on the cycle; see combos), and he dies with it if it is destroyed. He may also climb into a vehicle he has emptied, the game-wide takeover; in Zero Hour another Kell can then be trained (wiki).

abilities.name: Sniper Attack
abilities.summary: His one button besides the basic orders: a special round fired at one crewed enemy ground vehicle within his rifle's reach. The hull is not harmed, but its crew dies whatever the vehicle's armour or health, from a supply truck to an Overlord: the vehicle halts, turns neutral (grey) and runs no one over until an infantry unit climbs in and claims it for its owner, a game-wide rule, so his own troops can drive it away or the enemy can win it back. Riders of a sniped transport are pushed out within reach of his rifle, a sniped car bomb explodes, and a Combat Cycle is lost either way: blown up if it is moving, or left to scuttle once its rider is shot if it stands still. A construction dozer emptied this way and then claimed lets the GLA build the enemy's structures. Soldiers, aircraft, buildings and uncrewed machines such as the Sentry Drone take nothing from it. The shot gives him away like any attack, cannot be fired from inside a garrisoned building, and then takes about half a minute to be ready again.

abilities.name: Camouflage
abilities.summary: Always on, with no button: enemies can neither see nor target him, standing or moving, except while he attacks. Each rifle shot or snipe shows him, and a couple of seconds after he stops he vanishes again. An enemy detector close by uncovers him (Pathfinders, Sentry Drones, Listening Outposts, Radar Vans and several base defences), and both sides' announcers report it. Once he is uncovered, idle enemy units in range are sent after him. The same stealth lets him slip into a civilian building and shoot soldiers from it without the enemy noticing it is occupied (manual, tooltip, wiki), though enemy infantry who enter force him out. Coded as one passive with the cloak pattern, as the registry's Generals stealth note asks.

on_death.notes: In the sources he is simply gone: his Object file has death animations and no blast, so the infantry default applies, and since only one may live at a time a new Kell can be trained once he is dead. The Demolition General's side-wide Demolitions upgrade gives that general's version a button to blow himself up and a blast whenever he dies.

strengths.why: His build tooltip rates him strong against infantry: each rifle hit drops an ordinary soldier from a little over twice a rifleman's reach, and a campaign line has him taking soldiers out from long range.

Sniper Attack kills the crew of any crewed ground vehicle, from a supply truck to an Overlord, whatever its armour, and leaves the hull for his side's infantry to take (manual, wiki); the tooltip names vehicles as his other strength.
Enemies cannot see or target him until he attacks or a detector comes near, and he can hold a civilian building unseen while sniping soldiers from it (tooltip, manual).
His rifle reaches a little over twice as far as a Ranger's, so he can pick soldiers off from a distance and slip away before they close in (wiki).
As a commando he cannot be run over by ordinary enemy vehicles (wiki); only the Overlord and the Emperor crush heavily enough to flatten him.

weaknesses.why: His rifle cannot touch vehicles, aircraft, nearly any building or soldiers inside a garrison, so between snipes he has no answer to armour and none at all to fliers.

The snipe takes about half a minute to recharge, so it stops one vehicle at a time and a group overwhelms him, and enemy infantry can re-crew an emptied hull if his side is slow to claim it; he cannot snipe from inside a building either (wiki).

He wears an ordinary soldier's armour with only a little more health than a Ranger, taking double from enemy snipers and extra from flame, so once firing or a detector shows him he dies quickly, with idle enemies close by sent after him.
Only one Kell per player at a time, at a very high price, and only once a Palace stands.

countered_by.why: His build tooltip names scouts as his one weak point; the wiki explains that scouting units such as Pathfinders and Sentry Drones see through his camouflage and are deadly to soldiers, and the Pathfinder's rifle even outreaches his.

Any unit or base defence that detects stealth strips his only defence, and once seen he is a lone, fragile soldier for the rest of the enemy to shoot (wiki); hints name Sentry Drones and Listening Outposts as finders, and a campaign hint sends Listening Outposts against him.

The wiki explains that a machine with no crew shrugs off his snipe; it singles out the Sentry Drone, which his rifle cannot hurt either, and which also detects him, outruns him and keeps shooting him even while he rides a Combat Cycle.
The same reason: the wiki names the armed Sentry Drone, an uncrewed and faster stealth detector, as one of the gravest threats to him.
Nothing he carries can attack aircraft, so once he is revealed fliers can hit him freely (wiki).
In a group: his snipe takes one vehicle per long recharge and his rifle cannot hurt vehicles, so the rest of the group can shoot him down once he is revealed (wiki).

counters.why: Each rifle hit kills a basic soldier from well outside a rifleman's reach, Workers at GLA supply sites included (wiki), and he vanishes again soon after he stops firing; his build tooltip rates him strong against infantry.

One at a time: Sniper Attack takes any crewed ground vehicle out of the fight in one shot, from a supply truck to an Overlord, and leaves it for his side to capture; his build tooltip rates him strong against vehicles.
Sniping a transport's crew throws its riders out into the open, where his rifle picks them off (wiki).

Stinger Sites, the GLA's anti-air defences manned by soldiers: his rifle picks those soldiers off, silencing the site until other troops close in to destroy it (wiki); he also hurts a Fire Base and the troops inside it.

combos.why: Any soldier can climb into a vehicle he has emptied, so infantry close by turn each snipe into a stolen vehicle; the manual, a campaign hint and the wiki all pair him with GLA infantry for this.

Riding a Combat Cycle, whose rider sets its weapon, he keeps his rifle, his snipe and his stealth on a quicker mount that crosses rough ground and shields him from counter-snipers (official hint, wiki).
The same reason: the Combat Cycle is the bike he can ride, though the wiki warns that he dies with it and that it draws anti-armour fire.
He has no defence against aircraft, so the wiki advises keeping anti-air at hand wherever the enemy rules the sky.
A Radar Van with its Radar Scan upgrade can sweep his route for mines and hidden units, which he cannot detect himself (wiki).
While his snipe recharges, anti-vehicle units can destroy the detecting scout vehicles that would otherwise expose him (wiki).

units.memorable: A camouflaged mercenary sniper who picks off soldiers from afar and shoots the crew out of any enemy ground vehicle, Overlord included, leaving the hull for his infantry to steal.
units.as_player: The team's one hero pick at T3, a hidden marksman: invisible until you shoot, and seen for a moment after. Left mouse fires a precise long-range rifle that drops a soldier per hit but cannot hurt vehicles, aircraft or almost any building. Q (Sniper Attack) shoots the crew out of one enemy vehicle, leaving the hull neutral for any teammate on foot to take; it then recharges for about half a minute. Detectors, drones and aircraft are what hunt you.

sources.title: Command & Conquer: Generals – GLA Units, CNCNZ
sources.note: A long-standing fan site's unit list, cited as the second site in place of a third page of TheSuperHackers' repository, as the sources rule and the registry's CNCNZ note ask. Its Kell entry agrees on the price, the Palace, camouflage while he holds fire, unseen garrisoning, the one-per-player cap and a snipe after which any infantry may take the vehicle. It gives the snipe an instant cooldown and lists the demolition charges without naming the Demolition General (see uncertain). Read from the page cache's copy (fetched 2026-10-19).

uncertain.note: Medium comes only from the High or Medium tie-break over one point, the snipe's cooldown (abilities/0/cooldown), on which the cited CNCNZ page contradicts the wiki. The rest of the entry rests on cited official text (the manual, and the in-game tooltip through a faithful copy) and on pages that agree, and the 1.04 Weapon.ini backs the wiki on the cooldown, but game data is not official text, so it cannot settle the point. Left uncited, CNCNZ would not count and the entry would be high; the sources rule asks for it here as the second site, so the drop stands.

Roles step 1 reads the manual's Purpose entry, Scout and Base Infiltration. Both roles meet their requires (scout through the cloak passive's stealth-and-deception category), but neither has a target, so neither wins the bonus test and step 1 goes on; step 3 then gives marksman, because the main weapon is a sniper rifle that reaches long. The registry note reads every general's version as carrying the base-game Purpose entry, and all four Kell build buttons share one tooltip.

Scout and infiltrator both rank at roles.secondary step 1 (the Purpose entry), kept in the roles list's order. Two lower candidates are left out: anti-armour from the Sniper Attack button, which harms only vehicles (step 2), and anti-infantry from the rifle, which the tooltip calls strong against infantry (step 3). Infiltrator rests on Base Infiltration, on his hidden garrisoning and on the vehicle theft the snipe sets up; the roles tie-break keeps infiltrator for theft from inside, and Kell works from outside the vehicle while another soldier finishes the theft by climbing in, so that part of the fit is loose. The tooltip's weak line names scouts, but scout has no target and the registry's target words match scouts to no anti role, so the drop rule leaves it.

That every GLA general fields him rests on uncited 1.04 files of the same repository: CommandSet.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/CommandSet.ini) puts a Kell build button in each general's Barracks and gives the Toxin and Stealth Generals' copies the same Sniper Attack button and nothing more, and the generals' own objects in Object/ChemicalGeneral.ini, Object/DemoGeneral.ini and Object/StealthGeneral.ini need that general's Barracks and Palace, at the same price. The Zero Hour manual scan (https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/cnc_gamepedia_en/images/b/b1/CNC_Generals_Zero_Hour_Manual_2015.pdf/revision/latest, read, not cited) says the Toxin and Demolition Generals keep his camouflage though they lose their other stealth.

No climb trait: his own locomotor in the 1.04 Locomotor.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Locomotor.ini, read, not cited) moves only on ground and rubble, unlike the cliff locomotors the Generals notes give Colonel Burton and the Saboteur, and the wiki says a Combat Cycle lets him cross terrain he could not cross on foot.

The soldier rule compares his set with the basic rifleman's: that the Ranger and Pathfinder wear the same Human Armor rests on AmericaInfantry.ini of the unedited 1.04 files (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/AmericaInfantry.ini, read, not cited); the Rebel's object in the cited GLAInfantry.ini wears it too. The class itself comes from the armour_map (step 1).

Infantry and structures. The wiki's prose calls the rifle useless against most targets that are not infantry but leaves the Fire Base and the troops inside it open to it, and its trivia names the Fire Base as the one building that takes sniper damage, the rest being blocked. Armor.ini of the unedited 1.04 files (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Armor.ini, read, not cited) agrees: the vehicle, aircraft and nearly every building set take nothing from sniper damage, and the Fire Base set takes it in full. The Stinger Site's set lets it through as well, but a comment in the file says this is only so that snipers can kill the soldiers who man the site, which fits the wiki's praise of him against Stinger Sites, so the two pages do not clash. Structures fall outside the sniper family's target list, which the validator records as atypical; the entry rests on that one building type alone, and in practice the rifle works only against soldiers. The wiki's changelog adds that Generals patch 1.02 ended his one-shot kills of aircraft, without naming the weapon. The infobox's lore field calls the real rifle behind his gun anti-infantry; read as a label under can_target step 3 it would give the same list.

No cited page says how the shots travel, so hitscan is the sniper family's default; Weapon.ini in the 1.04 files (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Weapon.ini, read, not cited) agrees, giving the rifle no projectile and a speed that makes the hit effectively instant. It also has him fire twice as often as the Pathfinder's sniper rifle, which fits the wiki's word for his shots as quick.

That each hit drops a basic rifleman is reasoned from game data: the rifle's damage, doubled by Human Armor's sniper value (wiki infobox; Armor.ini, address under armament/0/can_target), is more than the Ranger's health in AmericaInfantry.ini (address under armour/class) and the Rebel's in the cited GLAInfantry.ini. The wiki says only that his shots pick off infantry with ease. CNCNZ says AP Bullets lets him drop an enemy commando with a single hit; by the same 1.04 figures a stock hit already seems enough for Colonel Burton, so that line may describe an older patch.

CNCNZ lists timed and remote demolition charges and a detonator among Kell's abilities on its GLA page. The wiki gives them only to the Demolition General's Kell, and the 1.04 files agree: the main command set in CommandSet.ini (address under tier) holds only the Sniper Attack beside the basic orders, and only the Demolition General's object in Object/DemoGeneral.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/DemoGeneral.ini, read, not cited) carries the charge abilities, which take several seconds to plant and reveal him. Abilities have no notes field, so the charges are left out of this list and named in tier.basis.

Several details rest on pages read but not cited. EA's Zero Hour source release (official): Source/GameLogic/Object/Body/ActiveBody.cpp (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electronicarts/CnC_Generals_Zero_Hour/main/GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Body/ActiveBody.cpp) leaves a sniped vehicle unhurt, unmanned, idle and on the neutral side, and blows up a moving Combat Cycle or, if it is parked, throws out and kills its rider so that the bike scuttles; Source/GameLogic/Object/Object.cpp (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electronicarts/CnC_Generals_Zero_Hour/main/GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Object.cpp) explodes a sniped car bomb and lets no unmanned vehicle crush anyone. Weapon.ini (address under armament/0/delivery) gives the crew-kill rifle the same reach as his rifle and one shot that reloads in about half a minute. Armor.ini (address under armament/0/can_target) lets every ground-vehicle set take the crew-kill damage in full, while the soldier, building, Sentry Drone, plane and Comanche sets take none. The forced exit of riders, the dozer trick and the ban on sniping from a building are on the cited wiki page.

The wiki infobox gives the snipe a recharge of about half a minute, and Weapon.ini in the 1.04 files (address under armament/0/delivery) agrees: the crew-kill rifle holds one shot and reloads it in that time. CNCNZ lists the cooldown as instant. Its cooldown field matches the reload times of special powers in the 1.04 SpecialPower.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/SpecialPower.ini), such as the Radar Scan and the Rebel's capture, while the snipe is a weapon button with no special power behind it, which may explain the gap. No official text gives the figure, so the band follows the wiki and the game data, and the High or Medium tie-break drops the entry to medium (see confidence).

hijack-vehicle, as research/registry-notes/patterns.md folds a snipe that kills a vehicle's crew into it: the snipe removes the crew so that the vehicle can be taken, while the taking itself is the game-wide rule for empty vehicles. execute-target (its ranged-shot variant) was weighed, since the shot takes one kind of target out of the fight whatever its armour, but the vehicle is not destroyed and either side can claim it afterwards, which is hijack-vehicle's interaction. The pattern's summary has the attacker take the vehicle over, which Kell never does himself (see fit_notes).

The stealth rules (hidden except while attacking, back after a short delay, idle enemies sent at him when revealed, hidden garrisoning, announcer events when he is found) come from his 1.04 Object file and the registry's Generals stealth note. The Garrisoning page of the Command & Conquer Wiki (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Garrisoning, read, not cited) says he and Pathfinders can garrison unseen and that soldiers inside a standing building are safe from their sniping; its Stealth page (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Stealth, read, not cited) lists the detectors, base defences among them, and says he lost his own detection in patch 1.03 of Zero Hour. The Zero Hour manual (address under tier) says the Toxin and Demolition Generals, who field no other stealth, keep his.

The Demolitions upgrade's effect on the Demolition General's version comes from uncited 1.04 files: Object/DemoGeneral.ini (address under abilities) gives his copy a suicide button and death weapons once the upgrade is bought, and CommandSet.ini (address under tier) adds the button. The registry's game-wide note treats the upgrade as side-wide, so it stays out of the outcomes.

That only the Overlord and the Emperor can crush him rests on his crushable level in the 1.04 object and on their higher crusher levels in ChinaVehicle.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/ChinaVehicle.ini) and TankGeneral.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/TankGeneral.ini), read with the engine rule the Generals game-wide notes give. The wiki says only that, being a commando, he is safe from enemy vehicles running him over.

The official Weak vs. line names scouts without saying which units it means; the reason follows the wiki, which singles out Pathfinders and armed Sentry Drones because they see stealthed units. That the Pathfinder's rifle outreaches his comes from Weapon.ini (address under armament/0/delivery), read, not cited.

The wiki names only the Sentry Drone as an uncrewed counter; Armor.ini (address under armament/0/can_target) shows that its armour set takes neither crew-kill nor sniper damage. Whether every other drone resists the snipe is not covered by the sources read.

fit_notes.wanted: a crew-kill variant: kill a vehicle's crew from range and leave the empty hull neutral for anyone to claim
fit_notes.note: The registry folds this snipe into hijack-vehicle, whose summary has the attacker take the vehicle over by removing its crew. Kell never takes it himself: the hull goes neutral, and the first soldier of either side to climb in gets it, so the victim's own infantry can win it back.

atypical.note: The rifle hurts one kind of building: the Fire Base takes sniper damage in full and so do the soldiers inside it (wiki; Armor.ini of the 1.04 files), while every other building is immune, so structures are listed although the sniper family leaves them out.

units.researched_by: batch r3, opening check (agents A and B, reconciled)

units.name: Battle Bus

tier.basis: Built at the Arms Dealer once the player owns a Palace: its 1.04 Object file lists both buildings as prerequisites, and the wiki infobox and CNCNZ name the Palace. The Palace is the GLA's single tech building, which the tier map puts at t3. All three Zero Hour GLA generals field it from their own Arms Dealer and Palace, so none lacks it, and every copy keeps the same seats, health and second life. Only two differ beyond price (see cost_band): once the Demolition General's side-wide Demolitions upgrade is bought, his copy gets a button to blow itself up, left out here because this entry follows the main GLA version; and the Stealth General's command set names a disguise button, but its next line gives that slot to an unload button and his bus has no disguise module, so it never disguises (the wiki's trivia says the disguise was dropped and does nothing if restored; see uncertain).

cost_band.basis: Its list price, the same in the wiki infobox, on CNCNZ and in its 1.04 Object file, falls between the medium and high thresholds, about a third above the mean price of the three anchor tanks, so medium. The Toxin General's copy costs a tenth more and the Demolition General's a fifth more (their 1.04 Object files), which would be high, but the registry bands the main faction's price; the Stealth General's costs the same.

mobility.notes: The wiki infobox gives a land speed three and a half times the Ranger's, so very fast: more than twice the Crusader tank's pace and a little quicker than a Humvee (1.04 locomotors; see uncertain), on four wheels. Zero Hour patch 1.03 made it slightly slower (wiki changelog), and like most units it slows down when badly hurt, a game-wide rule the band leaves out. A campaign briefing line in the game's text calls it slow-moving; a speed word alone does not set the band (see uncertain). It runs over enemy soldiers like every Generals ground vehicle (crusher level in its 1.04 Object file; the wiki lists the lines it calls out while running them down), though CNCNZ ties crushing to its second salvage step (see uncertain). As a bunker it never moves again (modes/0). Steer is the default for wheels.

body.notes: A reinforced civilian bus that looks more like a van (wiki), with its riders seated inside and firing from the windows: an enclosed troop compartment and no turret, so box-carrier. Medium, the size of trucks and APCs; no source gives its footprint. The first salvage step patches up its battered frame and the second fixes a ram to the front (wiki), changes of looks and armour only.

armour.notes: Step 4 of the armour-class steps decided (see uncertain): its set, Battle Bus Truck Armor (wiki infobox; 1.04 Object file), is one of the one-off sets the registry maps by what the unit is, and as an improvised armoured troop carrier it is an APC, which the class descriptions make medium. The set lets through only a quarter of gunfire, half of infantry rockets, flame and radiation, three quarters of jet missiles and most of a tank shell, while snipers, microwaves and melee do nothing to it (1.04 Armor.ini); its health matches a Battlemaster's. Each of its two salvage steps, from crates left by destroyed enemy vehicles, trims the damage it takes a little more (wiki): numbers only, so they stay here rather than as an ability. Junk Repair, a Black Market upgrade for every GLA vehicle, lets it mend itself slowly, even as a bunker (wiki): side-wide, so left off. It never ranks up, so the self-healing of the top ranks never reaches it. Each life has one health bar; the second life, a bunker with fresh, larger health and a building's armour set, is abilities/1 and modes/0 (see fit_notes).

sensors.notes: Its fog-clearing figure, the second sight figure in the wiki infobox and the one the registry uses, is half the Ranger's, so short, as the registry's sight note says for the Battle Bus. The first figure, how far it picks targets, is a quarter shorter still. Riders inside a transport see nothing (game-wide), so the bus's own sight is all its load gets. No sensor traits.

crew.notes: No player seats in the source, so solo is our proposal: the buyer drives. The bus has a driver of its own, whom Jarmen Kell's snipe can kill (wiki). Eight seats for infantry only (build tooltip; 1.04 Object file), copied from the source; riders fire their own weapons from the windows (manual, wiki), so passenger-firing. Angry Mobs cannot ride (Zero Hour manual), and a Pilot who climbs in just rides along, since the bus cannot be promoted (see uncertain). Riders keep their own upgrades (wiki).

abilities.name: Firing ports (passenger seats)
abilities.summary: Up to eight infantry ride inside and shoot their own weapons out of the windows, so what the bus can hit, how hard and how far depends wholly on who is aboard; empty, it cannot attack at all. Since Zero Hour patch 1.03 the riders can aim straight at aircraft, and a bus with anyone aboard can no longer be taken over by a Hijacker (wiki changelog). Riders keep their own upgrades. Loading, unloading and its Evacuate button are universal keys and stay off; what happens to the riders when the hull dies is abilities/1.

abilities.name: Bunker (second life)
abilities.summary: The first blow that would destroy the bus does not: it is flung into the air, comes down and stays put for good as a bunker, its health refilled to a larger pool and its armour swapped for a building's set (modes/0). Each rider loses half his full health, so healthy riders live on inside and keep firing. If it was empty, or everyone gets out, the hulk is gone within about a second; when the bunker falls, everyone still inside dies with it (wiki, CNCNZ; the manual and two campaign lines describe the bunker too). It happens once per bus.

modes.name: Bunker (after the first destruction)
modes.summary: Cannot move again. The hull becomes a fixed bunker with fresh health, more than half again the bus's, and a building's armour set: mines and Jarmen Kell's snipe no longer harm it, weapons that disable buildings now affect it while vehicle-disabling ones do not, and particle beams and Aurora bombs hit it twice as hard (1.04 Armor.ini). The riders stay inside and go on shooting; emptied, it breaks up within about a second, and destroyed, it kills everyone inside. Junk Repair, if bought, still mends it (wiki). Class and body stay the bus's (see fit_notes).

on_death.notes: No on-death term fits what the source shows: the first lethal hit turns a loaded bus into a bunker instead of killing it (abilities/1), an empty one is simply gone about a second later, and when the bunker falls every rider still inside dies, since its 1.04 Object file makes them lose all their health (the wiki agrees). Nobody gets out on their own and no unit repairs, recrews or salvages the remains, so the 3C proposal applies: bail-out, which is also how passenger-sets-weapon's wreck-bunker variant handles the player version, throwing everyone out hurt while the hull stays as cover (see fit_notes). The Demolition General's side-wide Demolitions upgrade gives his bus a blast when it is finally destroyed.

strengths.why: Up to eight soldiers shoot their own weapons out of its windows, so a mixed load of riflemen and rocket troops can be fitted to almost any enemy (wiki); its build tooltip rates it strong against infantry and buildings.
Eight seats put a whole load of infantry fire into one armoured hull that carries them to the front (manual, build tooltip).
Tough for a carrier: its hull lets through only a quarter of gunfire and has as much health as a Battlemaster, two salvage steps add more armour, and the wiki finds its mix of speed and armour sound.

Destroyed with riders aboard, it comes back as a parked bunker with fresh health, and the hurt riders go on firing from it until it falls, which the wiki finds handy for holding an isolated spot (manual, wiki).

weaknesses.why: All its firepower is its riders': empty it cannot attack at all, a load of Rebels alone is easy prey for vehicles and a load of RPG Troopers alone does little to infantry, and anything that outranges the riders, jets above all, can hit it without reply (wiki).
The bunker can never move again, everyone still inside dies when it falls, and once the riders get out it is gone within moments (wiki, CNCNZ).

Weapons that kill crews empty it: Jarmen Kell's snipe kills the driver and the riders spill out into the open, and neutron mines and shells kill riders and crew alike, leaving the bus free for the enemy to take (wiki).
It never ranks up (1.04 Object file; Pilot page), so unlike most units it never gains the extra health and self-healing that ranks bring, however many kills its riders make.

countered_by.why: The wiki calls it very weak against attack from a distance: units that outreach its riders' guns pick it apart without reply.
Jets strike it from far beyond its riders' reach before they can fire back, and the wiki rates them a match for, or better than, a fully loaded bus.
Jarmen Kell's crew-killing snipe kills its driver, which makes every rider get out, where they are easy to pick off (wiki).
The same reason: the wiki names Kell, whose snipe empties the bus.

Its Neutron shells kill the passengers and crew together and leave the bus open to capture, as Neutron mines also do (wiki); no word-list or pattern link names crew-killing shells, and most artillery cannot do this, so the unit link stands alone.

counters.why: Hijackers: since Zero Hour patch 1.03 they cannot take a bus while anyone is aboard (wiki changelog), so a loaded one is safe from them.
The same reason: the wiki's changelog names the Hijacker.

combos.why: Any soldier but an Angry Mob can ride and fire from the windows with his own weapon and upgrades; loaded, its build tooltip rates it strong against infantry and buildings (manual, wiki).
Rocket troops aboard answer enemy vehicles, which a load of Rebels alone cannot (wiki).
The same reason: the wiki names RPG Troopers.
Riflemen aboard deal with enemy soldiers, which a load of RPG Troopers alone handles badly (wiki).
The same reason: the wiki names Rebels.

units.memorable: A reinforced civilian bus whose eight riders shoot out of its windows, and which, when destroyed, slams down as a bunker they keep fighting from.
units.as_player: You drive a tough T3 bus with eight seats for teammates on foot, who shoot their own weapons out of the windows: the bus is as dangerous as its load, and alone you can only run soldiers over. When the hull is destroyed it crashes down as a parked bunker with fresh health, and your hurt riders fight on from it until it falls; anyone who climbs out leaves it to crumble. It never ranks up, so keep it loaded and away from long-range guns and jets.

sources.title: Command & Conquer: Generals - Zero Hour manual (2015 scan), hosted by the Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.note: EA's printed manual; the Command & Conquer Wiki hosts the scan. Its table of new GLA units on printed page 14 describes the Battle Bus as a reinforced civilian bus that takes infantry to the front, whose riders fire from the windows and which, once immobilised, shelters the troops still inside like a bunker; a note on the same page says Angry Mobs cannot be transported. Read in a layout text dump of the PDF; paraphrases checked by hand, since the copy-check cannot read it.

sources.title: Battle bus (Zero Hour), Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.note: Read through the MediaWiki API, from the page cache's copy (fetched 2026-10-19). Infobox: the three Zero Hour GLA generals beside the main faction, health for the bus and the bunker, both armour sets, price, build time, the Arms Dealer and Palace, land speed, both sight figures and Junk Repair. Prose: the only GLA transport whose riders fire from inside; the bunker it becomes when destroyed, its riders left at half health, their death when it falls and its loss once they get out; loads of Rebels, RPG Troopers or a mix; its counters (attack from range, Neutron mines and shells, Jarmen Kell, fixed-wing aircraft); the two salvage steps; the Zero Hour 1.03 changes (riders can target aircraft, a little slower, no hijacking while occupied). Its quotes include lines for crushing; its trivia covers the full repair as a bunker, the empty bus vanishing and the Stealth General's dropped disguise. A quote box copies the Zero Hour manual's description.

sources.title: generals.str, first plain-text copy of the Zero Hour 1.04 English string table, TheSuperHackers' GeneralsGamePatch repository on GitHub
sources.version: Zero Hour 1.04 (the file's first version, which matches the binary original)
sources.note: Copies the in-game text, as the registry note says; read from the page cache's copy (fetched 2026-10-20). All four Battle Bus build buttons in the unedited 1.04 CommandButton.ini of the same repository (main GLA, Toxin, Demolition and Stealth Generals) point to CONTROLBAR:ToolTipGLABuildBattleBus: it can take eight infantry and is strong against infantry and buildings, with no weak line. The campaign lines DIALOGEVENT:UnitDescriptXGLA027Subtitle and DIALOGEVENT:UnitDescriptXChina026Subtitle describe a carrier for eight infantry who fire out of it and whose hull stays behind as a bunker when it is destroyed; the first calls it slow-moving. MAP:MD-CHI05_Hint10 tells the player to stop Battle Buses before they reach the base, GUI:BioFeatures_GLA lists the Battle Bus among the GLA's Zero Hour features, and OBJECT:BattleBus gives its name.

sources.title: GLAVehicle.ini, unedited Zero Hour 1.04 game files, TheSuperHackers' GeneralsGamePatch repository on GitHub
sources.note: The bus's object, GLAVehicleBattleBus: display name, eight transport slots for infantry only, riders allowed to fire and given its weapon bonuses, two sets of dummy weapons and no real one, the bus and bunker armour sets with both salvage steps, price, build time, both sight figures, the Arms Dealer and Palace as prerequisites, crusher and crushable levels, the vehicle, transport and salvager kinds, health and second-life health, never trainable, self-repair behind Junk Repair, its locomotor, and the second-life death behaviour that throws it up, takes half of each rider's health and destroys the hulk once it has stood empty for a moment; riders lose all their health when it is finally destroyed.

sources.title: Command & Conquer: Generals - Zero Hour - GLA Units, CNCNZ
sources.note: A long-standing fan site's unit list, cited as the second site, as the sources rule and the registry's CNCNZ note ask. Its Battle Bus entry agrees on the price, the Palace, eight infantry firing from the windows and the bunker that shelters the troops still inside, and lists Evacuate, which wrecks the remains at once when the bus is immobilised. It says the bunker comes when the bus is badly damaged, and that the second of its two salvage steps lets it crush infantry (see uncertain). Read from the page cache's copy (fetched 2026-10-27).

uncertain.note: Medium comes only from the High or Medium tie-break over one point, the crush trait (mobility/traits), on which the cited CNCNZ page contradicts the cited 1.04 Object file, with no official text to settle it. The rest of the entry rests on cited official text (the Zero Hour manual, and the build tooltip and campaign lines through a faithful copy) and on pages that agree.

Crush follows the registry's game-wide rule: the bus's 1.04 Object file gives it, from the start, the crusher level every Generals ground vehicle has, and the wiki's quote list has lines it calls out while running soldiers down. CNCNZ says instead that only the second of its salvage steps lets it crush infantry; the wiki ties that step only to a ram and more armour, and in the Object file the step changes only the armour set. On a medium vehicle the trait breaks its size rule (atypical).

The band rests on the wiki infobox's land speed and the registry's Ranger figure. Locomotor.ini of the unedited 1.04 files (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Locomotor.ini, read, not cited) agrees with the wiki and gives the Crusader's and Humvee's figures that mobility.notes compares it with. The campaign line DIALOGEVENT:UnitDescriptXGLA027Subtitle in the cited string table calls it a slow-moving transport, which the figures do not bear out; by the speed-band rules a speed word alone stays in notes.

Step 4 needs the kind of unit, since the registry lists the Battle Bus among the one-off armour sets that map by what the unit is. Read as an improvised armoured personnel carrier (the manual's reinforced bus that carries infantry to the front and lets them fire from the windows; the wiki's heavy infantry transport and moving bunker), it is medium. Read as a civilian bus, nearer the class descriptions' trucks, it would be light, and the set's own name says truck. Toughness does not decide at step 4, but its health matches the Battlemaster's in ChinaVehicle.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/ChinaVehicle.ini, read, not cited), and its set lets through as little gunfire as the Tank Armor set does.

The set's values for the bus, the two salvage steps and the bunker come from Armor.ini of the unedited 1.04 files (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Armor.ini, read, not cited). The Salvaging page of the Command & Conquer Wiki (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Salvaging, read, not cited) lists the bus's two steps as better and better armour, as the cited Battle bus page does.

Step 1 finds no role: as a Zero Hour unit it has no Purpose entry, and the opening line of its build tooltip only says it takes eight infantry, which the registry note reads as naming no role. Step 2 applies because it carries no weapon of its own (its riders fire their own), and its main action, carrying infantry, is transport, which its eight seats allow. The campaign line DIALOGEVENT:UnitDescriptXGLA027Subtitle also calls it a transport.

Both rest on step 5, the riders, ranked by how many GLA infantry types give each: anti-infantry from Rebels and Jarmen Kell (and the Toxin General's Toxin Rebels), with the build tooltip's strong-against-infantry line behind it; anti-armour and anti-air each from the RPG Trooper alone, and marksman from Kell alone, so the tie goes by the order of the roles list and anti-armour takes the second slot. The sources show no fire from the windows by Workers, Hijackers, Saboteurs or Terrorists, so they add nothing. Anti-armour meets its requires only through the RPG Troopers' rockets, which the validator cannot see (atypical). The tooltip's buildings part matches no role. Area denial would fit the bunker, but its requires fail (fit_notes).

Empty, because riders who fire their own guns from ports give no weapon entries. Weapon.ini of the unedited 1.04 files (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Weapon.ini, read, not cited) shows that the two weapons in its Object file are dummies that do no real damage: they only let the bus take attack orders for its riders, one of them against aircraft alone, which fits the 1.03 change that let riders target aircraft.

That riders see nothing from inside is the registry's game-wide note, from EA's Object.cpp. The Hijacker change and air targeting come from the cited wiki's changelog; the 1.04 Object file passes the bus's own weapon bonuses on to its riders.

The second life's mechanics come from EA's released Zero Hour source code, read, not cited. Source/GameLogic/Object/Body/UndeadBody.cpp (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electronicarts/CnC_Generals_Zero_Hour/main/GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Body/UndeadBody.cpp) catches the first lethal hit, unless it is of a kind nothing resists, fully heals the bus to its second-life health and swaps in the second armour set. Source/GameLogic/Object/Behavior/BattleBusSlowDeathBehavior.cpp (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electronicarts/CnC_Generals_Zero_Hour/main/GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Behavior/BattleBusSlowDeathBehavior.cpp) throws it up, takes half of each rider's full health, holds it in place for good once it lands, and destroys it after it has stood empty for the delay its Object file sets, about a second, unless someone gets back in first. The sources name the trigger differently: the wiki says when destroyed, the manual when immobilised, CNCNZ when badly damaged; the code bears out the wiki. CNCNZ has its Evacuate button wreck the remains at once, the wiki shortly after.
Per-life: the second life comes once per bus and no source gives a wait.

Structure follows the cited wiki page and the Garrisoning page of the same wiki (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Garrisoning, read, not cited), which both say it becomes a structure, and the second-life armour set, a building's set in Armor.ini (address under armour/notes). The 1.04 Object file keeps the vehicle kind for the bunker form and the code adds no structure kind, so the game may still pick targets for it as for a vehicle.

How the generals' copies differ rests on uncited 1.04 files of the same repository: Object/ChemicalGeneral.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/ChemicalGeneral.ini), Object/DemoGeneral.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/DemoGeneral.ini) and Object/StealthGeneral.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/StealthGeneral.ini) give each copy that general's Arms Dealer and Palace, the same seats, health and second life, the Toxin and Demolition copies higher prices, and the Demolition copy a suicide weapon and death blasts behind the Demolitions upgrade. CommandSet.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/CommandSet.ini) puts a build button in each general's Arms Dealer, gives the Demolition copy its suicide button after the upgrade, and fills slot 1 of the Stealth copy's set first with a disguise button and then with an unload button; the Stealth object has no disguise module. CommandButton.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/CommandButton.ini) shows every version's build button using the same tooltip, so that text counts as official for every version.

That a Pilot can only ride in it rests on the Pilot page of the Command & Conquer Wiki (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Pilot, read, not cited), which counts Battle Buses among the transports that cannot be promoted.
Besides the cited Object file, which marks it as never trainable, the Pilot page (address under crew) says the bus can never gain a rank.

The wiki names Neutron mines and the Nuke Cannon's Neutron shells. No word-list or pattern link describes weapons that kill a vehicle's crew and riders and leave the hull, and most artillery cannot do it, so the unit link stands alone; the Nuke Cannon's id is the one its entry would get.

Counters holds only what the bus foils by itself, since it harms no enemy with a weapon or an ability of its own (Matchups rule 5): its tooltip rates it strong against infantry and buildings, but that fire is the riders', so it sits in combos. pattern:hijack-vehicle names the enemy in countered_by as well: a Hijacker trying to climb in is foiled, while Jarmen Kell's crew-killing snipe still empties the bus, two different situations.

The Rebel and RPG Trooper links rest on the wiki's advice about loads; their ids, like Jarmen Kell's, the Hijacker's and the Nuke Cannon's elsewhere in this entry, are the ones their entries would get.
None: the wiki says its design influenced the Reckoner of Kane's Wrath, but the names differ and no source presents the two as one unit.

fit_notes.wanted: a second-life outcome: the lethal hit turns the hull into a static bunker with fresh health whose riders survive hurt and keep fighting until it falls
fit_notes.note: No on-death term covers what the source shows. Wreck needs remains that a unit repairs, recrews or salvages, and leaves out remains that only give cover; bail-out needs crew or riders getting out on their own. The 3C default stands, and passenger-sets-weapon's wreck-bunker variant throws the players out hurt too.

fit_notes.wanted: a structure class and body plan for a vehicle's static bunker form
fit_notes.note: As a bunker it is a fixed fortification, which no unit class or body plan describes, so the mode keeps the bus's class and body.

fit_notes.wanted: a second-life armour model: a lethal hit starts one more, larger health pool in a new form
fit_notes.note: Each life has a single health bar, but the first life's lethal hit starts a second one in the bunker form; abilities/1 and modes/0 record it.

The bunker is a fortification left on the ground that riders fight from, which the wiki finds handy for holding an isolated spot, but area denial needs a lingering-zone weapon or an area or summon pattern, which the bus lacks.

atypical.note: Every Generals ground vehicle whose crusher level is above zero runs over soldiers, as the registry's game-wide note asks to code, and this one is medium, the size of trucks and APCs.

Anti-armour enters at roles.secondary step 5 through its riders: RPG Troopers firing their rockets from the windows meet the role's need for armour-piercing damage, which step 5 allows, but riders who fire their own guns give the bus no weapon entry, so the validator cannot see them.

units.name: Technical

tier.basis: Built at the Arms Dealer, the GLA's basic vehicle factory, with nothing else needed (its Prerequisites in the 1.04 files), so t1. Every GLA general fields it: the Toxin, Demolition and Stealth Generals' Technicals match the main one apart from the Demolition General's higher price (see cost_band).

cost_band.basis: Its list price is about two thirds of the main battle tank anchor, inside the low band. The Demolition General (Juhziz) pays a fifth more for his (wiki; the 1.04 files agree), which is still low.

mobility.notes: Its land speed is four and a half times the Ranger's and three times the Crusader's; the wiki ranks it with the speediest vehicles of all. It loses only a little speed when badly damaged. Like every ground vehicle it flattens soldiers in its path (crusher level in the 1.04 files), but it cannot run over other vehicles.

body.notes: An armed civilian pickup: the gun turns on a turret in the open bed, with its gunner standing exposed, while the riders are not shown. Salvage swaps the gun model for a cannon and then a rocket pod. It comes in three chassis models that play alike (wiki).

armour.notes: Step 1 of the armour-class steps decides: its Truck Armor set maps to light. The wiki calls it only lightly armoured and dependent on its speed. Junk Repair, a Black Market upgrade for every GLA vehicle, lets it mend itself slowly, and Technical Training, a general's promotion, makes new Technicals start at the first veterancy rank; neither is stock.

sensors.notes: The wiki lists a targeting figure and a larger fog-clearing figure; the fog figure, which the registry uses, is three quarters of the Ranger's.

armament.name: Heavy machine gun
armament.summary: A machine gun on a quick turret in the truck bed. It tears through soldiers and works on light vehicles but does little to tanks, and like both salvaged weapons it cannot shoot at aircraft (1.04 data). It reaches as far as a Ranger's rifle and half again. Armour-Piercing Bullets, a side-wide Black Market upgrade, add a quarter to its damage.

armament.name: Salvaged cannon
armament.condition: Taken from salvage: the first crate the truck picks up replaces the machine gun with it for the rest of its life.
armament.summary: A light gun firing single shells that burst over an area, far slower than the machine gun but better against lightly armoured vehicles (wiki). An early Generals patch moved its damage from explosive to a bullet class so that it would hurt tanks less, and the game still files its hits as gunfire, so heavy armour shrugs them off. Same reach as the machine gun. Armour-Piercing Bullets add a quarter.

armament.name: Salvaged rocket launcher
armament.condition: Taken from salvage: the second crate replaces the cannon with it for the rest of the truck's life.
armament.summary: A rocket launcher that hits vehicles harder still (wiki). Its rockets fly to the target, so point-defence lasers can shoot them down and the ECM Tank can throw them off course. It cannot fire at aircraft, nor at a target almost touching the truck (1.04 data). Same reach as the earlier guns. Since Zero Hour patch 1.03 Armour-Piercing Bullets raise its damage too.

crew.notes: Solo proposal: it fires one gun at a time. The wiki says the riders travel in addition to a driver and a gunner, a crew that exists only in the fiction and the models. The seats take infantry only; riders sit as cargo, since the truck has no firing ports (wiki).

abilities.name: Transport infantry
abilities.summary: Up to five soldiers ride inside. They cannot fire from the truck and have to get out to fight (wiki); Evacuate empties it at once. When the truck is destroyed they climb out alive but hurt.

abilities.name: Salvage
abilities.summary: When a GLA unit destroys an enemy vehicle, a salvage crate drops by the wreck; the Salvaging page says a GLA vehicle the enemy destroys leaves one as well. Only GLA players see the crates and only their GLA units can collect them, not captured vehicles of other sides (Salvaging page); crates vanish after about half a minute (1.04 data). Driving over one moves the Technical one step up a fixed ladder, whatever the wreck was: first a splash cannon replaces the machine gun, then a rocket launcher replaces the cannon. After both steps a crate gives a little money or, now and then, a veterancy rank; before that, crates never rank it up (Veterancy page). The upgrades stay on the truck if its crew is killed and someone else claims it.

on_death.notes: Only when riders are aboard: they get out alive but hurt. The wiki says they keep half their health; the 1.04 files take only a tenth of their health from them. An empty Technical is simply gone, and its crew from the fiction never climbs out. The Demolition General's Demolitions upgrade, bought once for his whole side, adds a detonate order; since patch 1.03 of Zero Hour his Technical blows up only on that order, not when it is destroyed (wiki).

strengths.why: Among the quickest vehicles in the game (wiki): it reaches an unready base early, runs from fights it cannot win and gets to salvage crates first.
Its gun cuts down soldiers: the build tooltip rates the Technical strong against infantry, and the manual says it does well against soldiers and lightly armoured vehicles.
Five soldiers ride in the back, so an early rush can drop a squad straight into a base that is not ready (wiki), and they live through the truck's death.
It grows with the wrecks its side leaves: two crates swap its gun for a splash cannon and then for a rocket launcher that hits vehicles harder (wiki, Salvaging page).
Cheap and built at the Arms Dealer with no further tech, so it is on the field early (wiki: affordable, early access).

weaknesses.why: Only lightly armoured: sustained fire kills it quickly, and it must rely on speed to get away (wiki).
None of its guns, stock or salvaged, can shoot at aircraft; the tooltip names aircraft as a weak point and the wiki calls it very vulnerable to them.

Its bullets, and even the salvaged cannon's hits, count as gunfire that heavy armour shrugs off: the tooltip calls it weak against tanks, and even upgraded it needs plenty of help against heavy vehicles (wiki).
Its riders are cargo with no firing ports: they cannot shoot from inside and must climb out to fight (wiki).
Its last salvaged weapon fires rockets that point-defence lasers can shoot down and the ECM Tank can deflect (wiki).

countered_by.why: Nothing it carries can shoot upward, and both the tooltip and the wiki single out aircraft as its bane.
Tanks: the tooltip lists them as a weak point, and the wiki says even a fully salvaged Technical needs a lot of support to beat heavy vehicles, while the manual rates it only against light ones.
Point-defence lasers can intercept the rockets of its last salvage step (wiki, Salvaging page), taking away the weapon it worked hardest for.

counters.why: The build tooltip rates it strong against infantry, and the manual calls its gun effective against them.
The manual rates it effective against light vehicles too, and its first salvaged cannon handles lightly armoured vehicles better still (wiki).

combos.why: Loaded with up to five soldiers, it turns a fast early rush into a troop drop inside a base that is not ready (wiki).
Anti-tank teammates deal with the tanks it cannot beat, and every enemy vehicle a GLA unit destroys leaves a crate the Technical can drive over for its next salvage step.

units.memorable: A cheap, very fast gun truck that loots the battlefield: crates from destroyed vehicles turn its machine gun into a splash cannon and then a rocket launcher, while five soldiers ride in the back.
units.as_player: A fast early pickup: left mouse fires a turret machine gun that shreds soldiers but not tanks, and nothing you carry hits aircraft. Drive over salvage crates only your team can see to swap in a splash cannon, then a rocket pod that point defence can swat down. Up to five teammates ride as cargo; they cannot shoot from the bed and spill out hurt if the truck is destroyed.

units.name: Overlord

tier.basis: Built at the War Factory once a Propaganda Center, China's one tech building, stands (Prerequisites in the 1.04 files; the wiki's infobox says tier 3). Of the Chinese generals, the Tank General (Kwai) builds the Emperor in its place, the Infantry General (Shin Fai) has no Overlord at all, and the Nuke General (Tao) fields his own version, which cannot get Uranium Shells or Nuclear Tanks (wiki).

cost_band.basis: Its list price is two and a half times a Battlemaster's, well above the very-high threshold. Each add-on is paid for separately, on the tank.

mobility.notes: Exactly as fast as the Ranger, which leaves it slower than the main battle tanks: four fifths of the Battlemaster's speed and two thirds of the Crusader's. The wiki calls it slow-moving and hard to manoeuvre. Unlike most units it keeps full speed when badly damaged (Locomotor.ini). It runs over enemy vehicles, tanks included, as well as soldiers: only it and the Emperor are heavy enough to crush other vehicles (wiki). Nuclear Tanks, a side-wide upgrade at the Nuclear Missile, makes it faster, and the Nuke General's version moves twice as fast as the stock tank.

body.notes: A four-track hull under one turret with twin cannons; the wiki stresses its sheer size and mass, and its collision box in the 1.04 files is twice the Battlemaster's length. A platform near the back takes one add-on, a bunker, a Gattling turret or a speaker tower, recorded under armament and abilities.

armour.notes: Its Tank Armor set maps to heavy (step 1), but check A makes it super-heavy: it is huge and t3, and the registry notes name it super-heavy by size. The wiki stresses its thick armour. An add-on has no health of its own and shares the tank's damage (1.04 files), and EMP or the ECM Tank disables tank and add-on together (wiki).

sensors.notes: The wiki lists a targeting figure and a slightly larger fog-clearing figure; the fog figure is half the Ranger's, so it clears the fog only a little past the reach of its own cannons. The Gattling Cannon add-on makes it a detector that reveals stealthed units around it (wiki), but that is an upgrade, so it stays out of the traits.

armament.name: Twin cannons
armament.summary: Two heavy shells fired close together from the main turret, then a pause before the next pair; each hit also hurts whatever stands right around the target. Strong against vehicles and buildings (tooltip), and it outreaches the main battle tanks' guns, but the turret turns slowly, the shells can stray against soldiers (1.04 data) and it cannot fire at aircraft. Uranium Shells, a side-wide upgrade at the Nuclear Missile, add a quarter to its damage; the Nuke General's version fires shells that leave radiation where they land (wiki).

armament.name: Gattling Cannon (add-on)
armament.condition: Added by the Gattling Cannon add-on, bought on the tank in the field; it rules out the other two add-ons.
armament.summary: A twin rotary bullet gun on its own turret on the tank's back that works just like China's Gattling Cannon base defence: its hits land instantly and it fires faster over a few seconds of shooting. It shreds infantry and aircraft and out-guns light vehicles but struggles against heavy armour, and it reaches nearly twice as far against aircraft as against ground targets. With it the tank also detects stealthed units. Chain Guns, a side-wide War Factory upgrade, add a quarter to its damage. Sitting near the rear, it reaches a little less far ahead and further to the sides and back (wiki).

crew.notes: Solo proposal: the stock tank fires one gun from its turret, and a gun added by an upgrade does not make a second seat. The five passenger seats come only with the Battle Bunker add-on, one of three that exclude each other; its riders fire out of it. The tank has a crew inside that Jarmen Kell can snipe, leaving it empty for any infantry to take (wiki).

abilities.name: Battle Bunker
abilities.summary: An add-on bunker built on the tank's back, bought on the tank in the field: five soldiers ride in it and fire their own weapons out, so the riders decide what else the tank can hit (Tank Hunters inside give it some anti-air cover, wiki). Unlike the standalone Bunker it gives no protection from chemical weapons. Evacuate lets them out; if the tank is destroyed they get out hurt. It rules out the other two add-ons.

abilities.name: Propaganda Tower
abilities.summary: An add-on speaker tower, bought on the tank in the field, that broadcasts to friendly units close around it, the tank itself included: they fire about a quarter faster and slowly heal or repair, at half the healing rate of China's static Speaker Tower. Allied players' units and aircraft benefit too, and several towers' bonuses do not stack. Subliminal Messaging, researched at the Propaganda Center, makes both effects stronger. It rules out the other two add-ons.

on_death.notes: Only with the Battle Bunker fitted and riders aboard: they get out with half their health gone (1.04 files). Otherwise it is simply gone. Nuclear Tanks, a side-wide upgrade, makes it explode when destroyed and hurt whatever stands near; the Nuke General's version blows up far more violently unless he researches Isotope Stability (wiki).

strengths.why: Thick armour lets it make the first breach in an enemy line and take the fire while lighter units follow (wiki).
One of only two vehicles in the game that can run over other vehicles, tanks included, which also clears crowds of small vehicles in tight spaces (wiki).
Its twin armour-piercing cannons make it a fine tank destroyer, and the build tooltip rates it strong against vehicles and buildings.

One add-on bought on the tank covers a gap of the player's choice: a bunker for firing soldiers, a Gattling gun against infantry and aircraft that also spots stealth, or a speaker tower that heals nearby units and speeds their fire (wiki).

weaknesses.why: Its cannons cannot fire at aircraft: the stock tank has no answer to them (wiki) and the tooltip names aircraft as a weak point; only a Gattling or a loaded bunker helps, and only somewhat.
Its turret traverses slowly, so large groups of smaller, more agile anti-tank units can overwhelm it (wiki).
Its shells are made for armour: the tooltip names rocket-armed infantry as a weak point, and the wiki calls it especially vulnerable to them.
A big, slow target: it moves at infantry pace, slower than the main battle tanks, so harassment, artillery and even plain dropped bombs wear it down on its way in (wiki).
It costs as much as two and a half Battlemasters, and the wiki warns never to send one alone.

countered_by.why: The stock tank cannot fire at aircraft: hit-and-run anti-armour planes such as the Raptor and the MiG destroy it while it can do very little back (wiki), and the tooltip names aircraft as a weak point.
Rocket-armed infantry, which the tooltip names as a weak point; the wiki calls it especially vulnerable to rocket-wielding soldiers.
Big groups of smaller, nimbler anti-tank units out-turn its slow turret and mob it (wiki).
Suicide attackers such as Terrorists and Bomb Trucks blow up when it tries to run them over, and a lone Overlord can neither kill nor outrun them before they reach it (wiki).
He snipes its crew and leaves it empty for the enemy to take (wiki). It stands alone because a sniper link would be false for most snipers, which cannot kill a vehicle's crew.
EMP weapons and the ECM Tank disable it and its add-on together; only riders in a bunker can still shoot back (wiki).

counters.why: Strong against vehicles by its tooltip: its twin cannons kill tanks, and it can simply drive over smaller vehicles (wiki).
Strong against buildings by its tooltip, and tough enough to make the first breach in a defended line (wiki).

combos.why: Works best in numbers with mixed add-ons: the wiki suggests a wedge of Overlords around one whose speaker tower heals the rest, and the Zero Hour manual an attack group of four, half fitted with Propaganda Towers and half with Gattling Cannons.
Tank Hunters riding in its bunker partly cover its blindness to aircraft (wiki).
Once it breaches the enemy line, smaller, faster and less armoured units go through to strike the rear and fight inside the base (wiki).
The Zero Hour manual keeps Nuke Cannons behind its Overlord group, because they are very good against buildings.

units.memorable: A huge twin-cannon tank that runs over other tanks and carries one add-on of three: a firing bunker, a Gattling that downs aircraft and spots stealth, or a speaker that heals and quickens allies.
units.as_player: A huge, slow tank with a slow-turning turret: left mouse fires twin armour-piercing shells, and you crush enemy vehicles by driving over them, but you cannot shoot aircraft. During a life you buy one of three add-ons: a bunker whose five seats let teammates shoot their own guns from your back, a Gattling turret that shreds infantry and aircraft and reveals cloaked enemies, or a speaker tower that heals you and speeds the fire of every friend around you.

Structures come from can_target step 4 (no source labels the gun by its targets, and the family allows buildings); no page says how it does against buildings.

The attack group of four comes from the Zero Hour manual's Full-Force Attack section, printed page 37 (https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/cnc_gamepedia_en/images/b/b1/CNC_Generals_Zero_Hour_Manual_2015.pdf/revision/latest), not a cited page; the wiki's wedge formation is cited.
Rests only on the Zero Hour manual's Full-Force Attack section, printed page 37 (same scan as above), which is not cited.

units.name: Red Guard

tier.basis: Trained at the Chinese Barracks with no other building: its 1.04 Object file lists only the Barracks as a prerequisite, the wiki infobox names no requirement, CNCNZ lists none, and the base-game manual counts it among the infantry the Barracks turns out. The Barracks is basic production, which the tier map puts at t1. The main Chinese side and the Nuke and Tank Generals field it, and their copies match the main one except for a higher price and a slightly longer training time. The Infantry General, Shin Fai, has no Red Guard: his Barracks trains the Mini-Gunner in its place, a unit of its own (generals.china-infantry.mini-gunner) that carries a rotary gun, also fires at aircraft and comes one per purchase (wiki, 1.04 command sets).

cost_band.basis: One purchase brings a pair of soldiers for well under half the anchor tanks' mean price and below the low threshold, so very low; the wiki infobox, CNCNZ (which gives the price per pair) and the 1.04 Object file agree on the list price. The Nuke and Tank Generals pay a little more for their pair, which is still very low.

mobility.notes: Its land speed in the wiki infobox, from a locomotor of its own in the 1.04 files, is a quarter higher than that of the Ranger and the Rebel, the speed reference, so medium. The wiki warns that it outpaces Tank Hunters, so mixed groups drift apart on the move. Like most units it slows down when badly hurt, a game-wide rule the band leaves out.

body.notes: Each purchase brings two riflemen, who leave the Barracks one after the other and then move and fight as separate units (1.04 Barracks production module, wiki, CNCNZ). Each takes one transport seat, and a Troop Crawler arrives with eight of them aboard.

armour.notes: Step 1 of the armour-class steps decided: its set is Human Armor (1.04 Object file; the wiki infobox writes HumanArmor), the set the Ranger and the Rebel wear as well, which the armour_map makes unarmoured, and the soldier rule keeps it there. It has two thirds of a Ranger's health. The set takes double damage from crushing and sniper fire, half again from flame and particle beams and only a tenth from tank shells and infantry missiles, and it gives no protection against toxins or radiation (wiki). One health bar; the healing of Elite and Heroic ranks belongs to veterancy. Red Guard Training, a one-star General's Promotion, makes every new Red Guard start as a Veteran; it is a side-wide power and stays off the bands.

sensors.notes: Its fog-clearing figure, the second sight figure in the wiki infobox and the one the registry uses, is half the Ranger's, so short, as the registry's Generals notes also list. Its first figure, how far it picks targets, equals its rifle's reach. It detects nothing hidden.

armament.name: Bolt-action rifle
armament.summary: Its one weapon: single rifle shots with a long pause between them, each hitting harder than a round from the Ranger's or the Rebel's assault rifle (wiki), and reaching exactly as far as the Ranger's rifle. Its Small Arms damage (wiki infobox) does full harm to soldiers but only a quarter to tanks and half to trucks and buildings, and it cannot be aimed at aircraft. While the horde bonus is active it fires half again as fast (abilities/0). From inside a garrisoned building it reaches further and hits harder, a game-wide bonus left off the band. The base-game manual promises a bayonet for close fighting, but it never made it into the game (see uncertain).

crew.notes: Bought in pairs, but the two riflemen act as separate units from then on, which the squad coding rule makes solo: one player is one rifleman.

abilities.name: Horde bonus
abilities.summary: Always on, with no button. When at least four other allied foot soldiers that carry the horde bonus themselves (Red Guards, Tank Hunters, or the Infantry General's Mini-Gunners) stand close around it, it fires half again as fast, and a red star appears beneath it. A Red Guard a little further out shares the bonus while it stays near one in the thick of the group. Other soldiers do not count, and Battlemasters horde only with each other. Troops who walk into a building keep the bonus they had on entering but cannot gain it inside. Nationalism, a side-wide upgrade bought at the Propaganda Center, raises it further.

abilities.name: Capture Building
abilities.summary: Every Red Guard gains this button, those already in the field included, once its side researches Capture Building at a Barracks. Sent at an enemy building or a neutral tech building, the Red Guard walks right up to it, unpacks a red flag and slowly raises it; if he finishes, the building and its function pass to his side, but moving him away or killing him first ends the attempt. The raise lasts longer than the button's own recharge, which runs after he is trained, after a capture and after a capture he abandons. Some structures cannot be taken, among them Palaces, Internet Centers, bunkers, Gattling Cannons, Fire Bases, Tunnel Networks, Stinger Sites, Patriot batteries and demo traps, and tech buildings can be captured only with this upgrade. A booby-trapped building explodes on him, and minefields around Chinese structures often foil captures (wiki).

on_death.notes: In the sources it is simply gone: its 1.04 Object file has only death animations and no blast, so the infantry default applies.

strengths.why: Its build tooltip rates it strong against infantry and the manual's Purpose line calls it anti-infantry; each rifle shot hits harder than a Ranger's or Rebel's, and pairs trained quickly wear enemy infantry down early (wiki).
One cheap, quick purchase gives two soldiers, so China can field them in numbers from the opening minutes (wiki, CNCNZ).
Packed together with four or more other horde soldiers, each rifle fires half again as fast (tooltip, manual, wiki), and Nationalism raises that further.

Once the Barracks upgrade is bought, Red Guards take over enemy buildings and neutral tech buildings; cheap, available early and unlimited in number, they can take over many more buildings at the same time than China's single Black Lotus (wiki).
In large horded groups they bring buildings down surprisingly fast for riflemen, a cheap stand-in when no Tank Hunters are at hand (wiki).

weaknesses.why: An ordinary soldier's armour with two thirds of a Ranger's health, so one Red Guard is a poor match for another side's infantryman (wiki); it has no protection from toxins or radiation, and fire hurts it extra.
Its rifle cannot be aimed at aircraft and does only a quarter of its damage to tanks, which is why its build tooltip names vehicles as its weak point.
It clears the fog only half as far as a Ranger (wiki infobox, game data).

countered_by.why: Its build tooltip names vehicles as its weak point: the rifle does only a quarter of its damage to tanks, and any enemy vehicle can run a rank-and-file soldier over.
Red Guards bunch up to keep their horde bonus, so area weapons such as the Ranger's flash-bang grenades dispatch them easily (wiki).
The wiki singles out the Ranger's flash-bang grenades, which tear through Red Guards bunched for their horde bonus.
Anti-infantry weapons cut them down quickly; the wiki names the Quad Cannon, the Gattling Tank and the Humvee.
It cannot fire at aircraft, so gunships such as the Comanche beat it from the air (wiki).
With no protection against toxins or radiation, chemical and nuclear weapons take a heavy toll on it (wiki).

counters.why: Strong against infantry by its build tooltip: massed early, cheap pairs overwhelm enemy foot soldiers by attrition, and they are the wiki's answer to GLA Terrorist rushes before China has a War Factory.
Named by the wiki: massed Red Guards stop Terrorist rushes, which China cannot otherwise answer well until it has a War Factory.
With the Capture Building upgrade, Red Guards take enemy buildings over instead of destroying them, and in large horded groups they also bring buildings down quickly (wiki).

combos.why: It works best in large groups (manual): with four or more other horde soldiers close by, each fires half again as fast (tooltip, wiki).
Red Guards count toward the Tank Hunters' horde bonus, a cheap way to keep it going and to hide the Tank Hunters in a crowd, while the Tank Hunters handle the vehicles the Red Guards cannot (wiki).
The partner the wiki names: mixed with Red Guards, Tank Hunters keep their horde bonus and are harder to single out, though the faster Red Guards must not be allowed to run ahead.
The Troop Crawler comes with eight Red Guards aboard and, loaded, suits a quick grab of key structures (manual, tooltip).
The transport the manual and the tooltip pair with it: it is sold with eight Red Guards inside.

units.memorable: China's cheapest soldier comes two to a purchase, shoots faster the more horde comrades crowd around him, and after one Barracks upgrade can raise a red flag over an enemy building.
units.as_player: A cheap rifleman with slow, heavy single shots that drop soldiers but barely dent vehicles and never reach aircraft. You fire half again as fast while four or more teammates on horde units stand close around you, so Red Guard players win by moving as a crowd and lose to grenades and flamers that punish crowds. Once the team buys Capture Building, holding Q at an enemy structure raises your flag over a long, exposed channel.
