sources.title: Command & Conquer: Generals – China Units, CNCNZ
sources.note: A long-standing fan site's unit list, cited as the second site in place of a third page of TheSuperHackers' repository, as the sources rule and the registry's CNCNZ note ask. Its Red Guard entry agrees on the price of a pair, no prerequisite, the horde bonus at five or more, training in pairs, the capture's recharge and its unlock at the Barracks, its exposure during a capture, and the Red Guard Training and Nationalism upgrades. It repeats the manual's bayonet, which the wiki says was never in the game (see uncertain).

uncertain.note: Medium comes only from the High or Medium tie-break over one point, the bayonet (see armament), on which the cited manual and CNCNZ contradict the cited wiki page. The manual is official text, but it was printed for the base game's release and describes a feature the wiki says was cut, and the 1.04 files agree with the wiki, so the entry follows them; that point decides whether the unit has a second, melee weapon entry. The rest rests on cited official text (the manual and the in-game tooltip through a faithful copy) and on pages that agree.

The base-game manual (printed page 34) has the Red Guard swapping his rifle for a bayonet in close fighting, and CNCNZ repeats it. The wiki's trivia says the bayonet stab was planned but never implemented. The 1.04 files side with the wiki: the cited Object file gives the Red Guard a weapon set with the rifle alone and keeps only bayonet animations, its command set in CommandSet.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/CommandSet.ini, read, not cited) has no bayonet button, and Weapon.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Weapon.ini, read, not cited) defines a bayonet weapon that no weapon set uses. So no bayonet entry is recorded.

Small arms by the weapon-families tie-break (rifles are always small arms): the manual and the wiki call it a bolt-action rifle, and Weapon.ini (address under armament) fires single shots with a long pause between them and no clip. The weapon's internal name in the 1.04 files calls it a machine gun, which the families rule ignores, since they go by how a weapon fires.

Infantry, ground vehicles and structures by can_target step 4: no source labels the rifle by its targets. That it cannot fire at aircraft is the wiki's statement for all basic infantry but the Mini-Gunner. The reduced damage to tanks, trucks and buildings comes from Armor.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Armor.ini, read, not cited), and the wiki says massed Red Guards bring buildings down.

No cited page says how the shots travel, so hitscan is the small-arms default; Weapon.ini (address under armament) agrees, giving the rifle no projectile and a speed that makes each hit effectively instant.

That each shot hits harder than a Ranger's or a Rebel's round is the wiki's statement; Weapon.ini (address under armament) gives the Red Guard's rifle three times the damage of the Ranger's per shot, though it fires far less often. The garrison bonus is a game-wide rule from the registry's Generals notes.

Who counts toward the horde rests on EA's Zero Hour source code, HordeUpdate.cpp (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electronicarts/CnC_Generals_Zero_Hour/main/GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/HordeUpdate.cpp, official, read, not cited): it counts only allied objects within the module's radius that carry a horde module themselves and match its infantry kind, needs one fewer than the module's count of five, and lets a unit within the wider rub-off reach of a full member share the bonus. The wiki's Horde Bonus page (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Horde_Bonus, read, not cited) agrees that any mix of Red Guards, Mini-Gunners and Tank Hunters counts and Battlemasters do not, and gives the bonus as half again the rate of fire, as GameData.ini does (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/GameData.ini, read, not cited). The registry's Generals game-wide note words it as four other allied soldiers of any kind; by the code, soldiers without the module do not count. The rule for troops in buildings comes from the Garrisoning page (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Garrisoning, read, not cited).

Several details rest on pages read but not cited. The Capture building page of the Command & Conquer Wiki (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Capture_building): the slow raise, the attempt ending if the unit moves or dies, when the recharge runs, the list of structures that cannot be captured, the minefield advice and the upgrade's price and research time, which Upgrade.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Upgrade.ini) confirms. EA's source code, Player.cpp (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electronicarts/CnC_Generals_Zero_Hour/main/GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/Common/RTS/Player.cpp, official): a finished upgrade of the player makes every object of that player recheck its upgrade modules, so Red Guards already in the field gain the button, which is why upgrade-in-field is linked. SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp in the same release (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electronicarts/CnC_Generals_Zero_Hour/main/GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp, official): a booby-trapped target goes off. The Zero Hour manual scan (https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/cnc_gamepedia_en/images/b/b1/CNC_Generals_Zero_Hour_Manual_2015.pdf/revision/latest, official, printed page 16): tech buildings need the Capture upgrade.

The recharge comes from SpecialPower.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/SpecialPower.ini, read, not cited), which gives the Red Guard's capture power a fifteen-second reload, and the cited CNCNZ page lists the same. The figure sits exactly on the edge between short and medium, and a value on an edge takes the higher band.

Roles step 1 reads the base-game manual's Purpose entry: Anti-Infantry names anti-infantry, which has no requires, and Urban Terrain Acquisition names no role (registry note), so step 1 gives anti-infantry. The registry reads every general's version as carrying the base-game Purpose entry, and the main, Nuke and Tank Generals' build buttons share one tooltip, which also calls it strong against infantry.

Engineer ranks at roles.secondary step 5: it rests on the Capture Building upgrade, with which Red Guards take over enemy buildings and keep them, and take neutral tech buildings too, which the engineer tie-break asks for. No button every copy has, no weapon and no speed, armour or senses give another role; the tooltip's weak line (vehicles) rules out anti-armour in any case.

Which generals field it rests on uncited 1.04 files of the same repository: CommandSet.ini (address under armament) puts a Red Guard build button in the main, Nuke and Tank Generals' Barracks and the Mini-Gunner in the Infantry General's, and the generals' own objects in Object/NukeGeneral.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/NukeGeneral.ini) and Object/TankGeneral.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/TankGeneral.ini) need only their Barracks, at a higher price and with a slightly longer training time. The Mini-Gunner's details come from the cited wiki page and Object/InfantryGeneral.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/InfantryGeneral.ini, read, not cited).

Two per purchase: the wiki and CNCNZ say Red Guards are trained in pairs, and the Barracks' production module in Object/FactionBuilding.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/FactionBuilding.ini, read, not cited) doubles each Red Guard order and lets them out one at a time.

The Ranger's health comes from AmericaInfantry.ini of the same 1.04 files (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/AmericaInfantry.ini, read, not cited), which also has the Ranger wearing Human Armor; the set's values come from Armor.ini (address under armament/0/can_target).

The vehicle matchup rests on the tooltip's weak line. The crushing part is reasoned: the cited Object file gives the Red Guard the squish module of rank-and-file soldiers, which by the engine rule in EA's Object.cpp (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electronicarts/CnC_Generals_Zero_Hour/main/GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Object.cpp, read, not cited) any crushing vehicle flattens, as the registry's Generals notes say.
The Terrorist is not coded yet; its id is built from its in-game name in the cited string table (OBJECT:Terrorist).

That Red Guards and Tank Hunters horde together rests on the wiki and on HordeUpdate.cpp (address under abilities/0); the wiki's strategy text also has Red Guards keeping Battlemasters horded, which the code and the Horde Bonus page contradict, so that part is left out.

fit_notes.wanted: a pattern for a group bonus that each member earns by standing close to enough others of its kind (a horde or swarm bonus), with no unit that hands it to the rest
fit_notes.note: As the registry's Generals notes say, rally-allies does not fit, because no single unit raises the others: every horde soldier checks its own neighbours. research/registry-notes/patterns.md folds the horde bonus into rally-allies, but that pattern's summary (an aura or a timed call from one unit) wins over the note.

units.name: Hacker

tier.basis: Trained at the Chinese Barracks once a Propaganda Center stands: his 1.04 Object file lists both buildings as prerequisites, the wiki infobox gives tier 3 and names the Propaganda Center, CNCNZ names it too, and the base-game manual tags him Structure Upgrade, a unit the tech building opens. The Propaganda Center is China's tech building, which the tier map puts at t3. The main Chinese side and all three Chinese generals field him; the Nuke General's copy matches the main one and the Tank General's costs more. The Infantry General, Shin Fai, fields a version that its build button calls the Super Hacker, otherwise the same unit: it is camouflaged, hidden from enemies except while it uses a hack, and idle enemies close by go for it when it shows itself; it starts at Veteran like all of that general's soldiers; it earns a little faster inside an Internet Center; its armour lets less toxin, radiation and microwave harm through; and it has a third button, Vehicle Hack, which knocks an enemy vehicle out for a while without having to stay at it (tooltip, 1.04 files, wiki; see uncertain).

cost_band.basis: The main faction's list price is about four fifths of the anchor tanks' mean price, at or above the low threshold and below medium, so low; the wiki infobox, CNCNZ and the 1.04 Object file agree on it. The Tank General pays about a quarter more for his, a medium price, but a general's surcharge counts only for a unit recorded under that general; the Nuke and Infantry Generals pay the main price (1.04 files).

mobility.notes: His land speed in the wiki infobox comes from the basic human locomotor of the 1.04 files, the Ranger's own, and the Ranger is the speed reference, so medium. Hack Internet plants him with his laptop out until he packs up again (see modes), hence the deploy trait. Like most units he slows down when badly hurt, a game-wide rule the band leaves out.

body.notes: A lone soldier carrying a laptop, which he unpacks on the ground to hack; he takes one transport seat (1.04 Object file).

armour.notes: Step 1 of the armour-class steps decided: he wears Human Armor (1.04 Object file; the wiki infobox writes Human), the Ranger's set, which the armour_map makes unarmoured, and the soldier rule keeps him there. He has a little over half a Ranger's health. The set takes double damage from crushing and sniper fire and half again from flame, and the wiki stresses that he has no protection at all from radiation or toxins. One health bar; the healing of Elite and Heroic ranks belongs to veterancy. The Infantry General's version wears that general's own soldier set, which lets less poison, radiation and microwave harm through but the same gunfire, so the soldier rule leaves it unarmoured as well.

sensors.notes: His fog-clearing figure, the second sight figure in the wiki infobox and the one the registry uses, is three quarters of the Ranger's, so medium. His first figure, how far he picks targets, equals the reach of his building hack. He detects nothing hidden. The Infantry General's version is camouflaged (see tier).

crew.notes: One soldier and one player, who works both hacks himself.

abilities.name: Disable Building
abilities.summary: Sent at an enemy building, he walks within a short reach of it, half again as far as a Ranger's rifle reaches, stops, spends several seconds unpacking his laptop and a few more getting ready, then plants a computer virus in it: the building is knocked out, together with the units and structures that depend on it (manual), for as long as he stays at the hack, and it comes back to life a couple of seconds after he stops, is killed or is given another order. He stands still and exposed the whole time (CNCNZ), and unlike his Internet hack it earns him no experience. From inside a garrisoned building he cannot use it, except in an Internet Center (wiki). The button is ready again almost at once.

abilities.name: Hack Internet
abilities.summary: He sits down wherever he stands, takes several seconds to unpack his laptop and then draws money out of the world economy online: a small payment reaches his side every couple of seconds for as long as he stays set up (1.04 data; see uncertain). Any new order makes him pack up first, which takes a few seconds. Hacking is how he ranks up: each payment earns him a little experience, so he climbs to Veteran, Elite and Heroic without fighting, and each rank raises the sum per payment until a Heroic Hacker brings in twice what a new one does. He can also hack from inside an Internet Center, a Zero Hour building that holds up to eight Hackers, and earns slightly faster there (hint, wiki); inside any other building he cannot (wiki).

modes.name: Hacking the Internet
modes.summary: Laptop out and hacking, he cannot move: any order makes him pack up first, which takes a few seconds. He keeps the same armour and health, stays an infantry target in the open, and keeps earning until he packs up or dies.

on_death.notes: In the sources he is simply gone: his 1.04 Object file has only death animations and no blast, so the infantry default applies.

strengths.why: His Purpose line in the manual is collecting funds: set up with his laptop he keeps money coming in for China anywhere, faster inside an Internet Center (hint) and more per payment as he ranks; the wiki rates a Heroic Hacker a better earner for his price than the Black Market or Supply Drop Zone.

His build tooltip rates him strong against buildings: from a short distance he puts an enemy building out of action, with what depends on it (manual), without destroying it, and keeps it that way for as long as he stays at the hack (wiki).

weaknesses.why: A soldier's armour, a little over half a Ranger's health and no weapon of any kind, so he cannot fight back at all (wiki), and his build tooltip names infantry and vehicles as his weak points; toxins and radiation hurt him freely.
While hacking the Internet he sits still with his laptop out and has to pack it up, which takes a few seconds, before he can run, so enemies who reach him catch him (CNCNZ, 1.04 files).
To shut a building down he has to come within a short reach of it and stay put, exposed, for the whole hack (CNCNZ), and the building recovers soon after he stops or dies.

countered_by.why: His build tooltip names infantry as a weak point: any enemy soldier can shoot him down unopposed (wiki), and the wiki warns that the GLA's Rebel Ambush power can wipe out a whole group of Hackers.
His build tooltip names vehicles as a weak point: he has nothing to stop them, and the wiki notes that vehicles simply run Hackers over.
With no protection at all from radiation or toxins, chemical and nuclear weapons kill him quickly (wiki).
Unarmed, he cannot touch aircraft, and the wiki's page on the Infantry General's version counts aircraft among the attackers that strike Hackers from beyond their reach.

counters.why: Strong against buildings by his build tooltip: he keeps an enemy building out of action, together with what depends on it (manual), for as long as he keeps hacking it, without having to destroy it.

combos.why: They do best together: the Zero Hour manual says an Internet Center takes up to eight Hackers, who work better as a group, and that a few of them inside bring in plenty of money.
A reasoned escort: his build tooltip names infantry as a weak point and the wiki says Hackers need protecting at all times, so troops that clear soldiers keep enemy infantry off him while he works.
A reasoned escort for his other weak point by the tooltip, vehicles: anti-tank troops or vehicles stop the enemy vehicles that would run him down while he hacks.

units.memorable: China's unarmed hacker sits down with a laptop to siphon cash off the Internet, earning more as hacking ranks him up, or keeps an enemy building switched off for as long as he stays at it.
units.as_player: You carry no gun at all. Plant your laptop anywhere to trickle money into your team's account, more per payment as hacking ranks you up, but you cannot move until you pack up again. Or hold Q at an enemy structure from a few steps away to keep it shut down while you stand exposed beside it, so your team has to guard you from soldiers and vehicles.

sources.title: Command & Conquer: Generals – China Units, CNCNZ
sources.note: A long-standing fan site's unit list, cited as the second site in place of a third page of TheSuperHackers' repository, as the sources rule and the registry's CNCNZ note ask. Its Hacker entry agrees on the price and the Propaganda Center, describes both hacks (close range, standing still and exposed while he works), lists their recharges and the income at each rank, and repeats the manual's description. It gives the starting income per second and quicker payments at each rank, which the 1.04 data do not show (see uncertain).

uncertain.note: High: the cited sources include official text about the unit, the manual's row and the in-game build tooltip through a faithful copy, and two established sites, the wiki and CNCNZ, describe him and agree on the rest. The points on which pages contradict each other, how fast the Internet payments come and how soon the building hack's button is ready again, decide no term (see abilities/1 and abilities/0/cooldown).

Roles step 1 reads the base-game manual's Purpose entry, Collect Funds and Neutralise Enemy Structures. As the registry's Generals notes ask, Collect Funds is read as a word form of collector, an alias of logistics, since he earns the money by his own action; Neutralise Enemy Structures names no role. Logistics has no requires, so step 1 gives it. The registry reads every general's version as carrying the base-game Purpose entry, and the main, Nuke and Tank Generals' build buttons also share one tooltip.

Infiltrator ranks at roles.secondary step 2 on the Disable Building button, which every version has: the role's description names shutting down buildings. The engineer, infiltrator and logistics tie-break asks for sabotage from inside; he works from a short distance rather than going in, planting a computer virus in the building's systems (tooltip), which is read here as sabotage from inside those systems. Disabler is no candidate: no weapon trait, damage type or control pattern meets its requires, and its tie-break makes it a role for acting on units. Engineer would need buildings he takes over and keeps, which he never does. The tooltip's weak line (infantry, vehicles) rules out anti-infantry and anti-armour in any case.

Which generals field him and how their versions differ rests on uncited 1.04 files of the same repository. CommandSet.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/CommandSet.ini, read, not cited) gives the main, Nuke and Tank Generals' Barracks a Hacker build button and the Infantry General's a button for his own version, whose command set adds Vehicle Hack. Object/NukeGeneral.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/NukeGeneral.ini, read, not cited) and Object/TankGeneral.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/TankGeneral.ini, read, not cited) give their copies the same prerequisites, the Tank General's at a higher price. Object/InfantryGeneral.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/InfantryGeneral.ini, read, not cited) gives Shin Fai's version that general's soldier armour, a Veteran start, innate stealth that its hacks switch off and that sends idle enemies after it when it shows, the vehicle hack and a quicker payout inside an Internet Center. The wiki's Super hacker page (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Super_hacker, read, not cited) and that version's build tooltip in the cited string table agree, and the string table's hint HELP:InfantryHacker-01 says that general's Hackers hack money faster.

The cited pages disagree on how the payments speed up. The wiki says each rank pays a larger sum at a faster rate, a Heroic Hacker paying every second, and CNCNZ gives the starting sum per second and shorter intervals at each rank. The cited 1.04 Object file gives one fixed wait between payments, a little shorter inside a building, with only the sum changing by rank, and EA's Zero Hour source code, HackInternetAIUpdate.cpp (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electronicarts/CnC_Generals_Zero_Hour/main/GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/AIUpdate/HackInternetAIUpdate.cpp, official, read, not cited), uses that wait at every rank, the shorter one only while he sits inside a building, and packs him up before any new order. The summary follows the game data; no term depends on the rate. The money thresholds for each rank that the wiki and CNCNZ give match the cited Object file's experience steps at one point per payment. The Internet Center details rest on the wiki's Internet center page (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Internet_center, read, not cited: up to eight Hackers, slightly faster, one per player) and on the Zero Hour manual scan (https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/cnc_gamepedia_en/images/b/b1/CNC_Generals_Zero_Hour_Manual_2015.pdf/revision/latest, official, read, not cited: printed page 12).

How the shutdown runs rests partly on an uncited page. EA's source code, SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electronicarts/CnC_Generals_Zero_Hour/main/GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Update/SpecialAbilityUpdate.cpp, official, read, not cited), keeps a lasting hack firing again and again until he dies, the target dies or he gets a new order, and skips allied targets; each firing keeps the building down for the effect time in the cited Object file, so it recovers a couple of seconds after the last one. The cited Object file also gives the reach, the set-up and preparation times and no experience for triggering it. The wiki speaks of paralysing certain enemy structures and names none that resist; which ones cannot be hacked was not checked.

SpecialPower.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/SpecialPower.ini, read, not cited) gives the building hack a half-second reload, while the cited CNCNZ page lists a few seconds; both are under five seconds, so spam either way.

The mode rests on the cited Object file's set-up and pack-up times for the Internet hack, on the wiki (he stays where he set up until the hacking stops) and on HackInternetAIUpdate.cpp (address under abilities/1), which makes him pack up before carrying out any new order.

The crushing part rests on the wiki and on the cited Object file, which gives him the squish module of rank-and-file soldiers; by the engine rule in EA's Object.cpp (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electronicarts/CnC_Generals_Zero_Hour/main/GeneralsMD/Code/GameEngine/Source/GameLogic/Object/Object.cpp, official, read, not cited) any crushing vehicle flattens such a soldier, as the registry's Generals notes say.

Aircraft rest on the wiki's Super hacker page (address under tier), which counts aircraft and long-range attacks among the threats that hit the Infantry General's version from outside its reach and says that version otherwise behaves like the ordinary Hacker, and on his lack of any weapon, which matchups rule 5 puts here.

units.name: Aurora Bomber

tier.basis: Built at the USA Air Field once a Strategy Center stands: its 1.04 Object file lists both buildings as prerequisites, the wiki infobox and CNCNZ name the Strategy Center, and the base-game manual tags it as a unit that building unlocks. The Strategy Center is the USA's single tech building, which the tier map puts at t3. Like every plane it also needs a free landing pad at the Air Field before it can be built (wiki; game-wide). Of the Zero Hour generals, the Laser General fields the same Aurora, and the Air Force General (Malcolm Granger) fields a cheaper, tougher one with a point-defence laser that shoots down incoming missiles and adds no button; both keep the plain Aurora Bomber name and the standard bomb (1.04 files, wiki). The string table also holds a Fuel-Air Aurora Bomber name under a label for Granger's object, but no object uses it: his fuel-air Aurora was cut before release (wiki trivia), and only unused fuel-air bomb objects remain in his file. The Superweapon General (Alexis Alexander) lacks it: his Air Field builds the Aurora Alpha Bomber instead, a unit of its own whose fuel-air bomb bursts twice, the second blast the larger (see uncertain).

cost_band.basis: Its list price, the same in the wiki infobox, on CNCNZ and as the build cost in its 1.04 Object file, is far above the very-high threshold and a little over three times the mean price of the three anchor tanks; the wiki says no unit in the game costs more. The Air Force General's version costs a fifth less and still bands very high (1.04 file, wiki).

mobility.notes: Its normal flying speed, in the wiki infobox and its 1.04 locomotor, is nine times the Ranger's land speed, so very fast. Among the game's planes it cruises a shade faster than the Raptor and the Stealth Fighter and half again as fast as the Comanche helicopter. On an attack run it switches to a supersonic locomotor more than two and a half times its cruise, nearly three times the Raptor's speed; once the bomb is away it slows at once and flies home on a sluggish locomotor a little slower than its cruise, the Chinook's pace (wiki infobox; 1.04 files). Its build tooltip says instead that its speed drops to half after the attack (see uncertain). Badly damaged it flies a third slower, a game-wide rule the band leaves out. A fixed-wing jet that cannot hover and lands only on an Air Field pad, so it attacks in passes, and the jet's default handling stands.

body.notes: A delta-winged jet bomber; planes are large by the size examples (jets).

armour.notes: Step 1 of the armour-class steps decided: its set is Airplane Armor (wiki infobox; 1.04 Object file), which the armour_map makes light. Its health is low: half a Raptor's, two thirds of a Stealth Fighter's and less than half a Ranger's (1.04 files). The set takes a fifth more than full damage from small arms, gattling guns and infantry missiles, a quarter from jet missiles, poison and radiation, and nothing from lasers, sniper fire or crew-killing shots (1.04 Armor.ini). One health bar; the self-healing of Elite and Heroic ranks belongs to veterancy and stays off. The Countermeasures upgrade, bought once at the Air Field for every USA aircraft (side-wide), gives it a set that takes less from gunfire and blasts and fires flares that divert part of the missiles aimed at it (the wiki says half of them; see uncertain). The Air Force General's version has half again the health and a point-defence laser that shoots incoming missiles down, the interceptor model on that version only.

sensors.notes: Its fog-clearing figure, the second sight figure in the wiki infobox and its 1.04 ShroudClearingRange, is exactly half again the Ranger's, on the edge between medium and long, which goes to medium; the registry's Generals notes name it among the farthest-seeing units any factory builds. Its first figure, the distance at which it picks targets, clears no fog. No sensor trait: it neither detects hidden units nor hides from view.

armament.name: Aurora bomb
armament.summary: One heavy bomb per sortie, let go on the supersonic attack run from about three times a rifle's reach short of the target and carried on ahead onto the target point; a comment in the 1.04 weapon file says the reach is set high because the plane flies so fast. Its blast hurts everything in a wide area (wiki; the infobox gives a radius and the Aurora Bomb damage name), and the wiki ranks it among the most destructive single weapons in the game. Being no missile, it cannot be jammed or shot down in flight, but it falls where it was aimed and does not follow a target that keeps moving, so a fast vehicle can drive out of the blast; it suits buildings, vehicles that have stopped or bunched up, and slow tanks such as the Overlord (wiki). It cannot attack aircraft. The 1.04 weapon file also lets the blast hurt friendly units, which only that file says, so no friendly-fire trait is set. After the drop the plane flies back to its Air Field and reloads the bomb on its pad in a few seconds (the limited-ammo resource). Granger's version carries the same bomb; the wiki's prose calls it a fuel-air bomb, while its infobox lists a single conventional bomb, and the two-stage fuel-air bomb belongs to Alexander's Aurora Alpha Bomber (see uncertain).

crew.notes: One plane with a pilot, who parachutes out once it holds a rank (see on_death); a player version is a lone pilot who flies and bombs.

abilities.name: Supersonic attack
abilities.summary: No button: every attack run switches it to supersonic flight, more than two and a half times its cruising speed, and for that run enemy fire cannot touch it (build tooltip, manual, CNCNZ). In the 1.04 files attackers aim at a point behind it and miss, and it stays untargetable for a couple of seconds after the bomb is away, so its strike all but surely lands (wiki). Only a wide blast going off right beside it, such as an EMP missile bursting nearby, can still hurt it on the run (wiki), and the manual warns that ground fire can reach Auroras flying in a large group. The price comes at once: with the bomb released it slows down and heads home at its sluggish speed, below its cruise, open to every kind of anti-air fire and to fighters (tooltip, manual, wiki). Coded as become-invulnerable; the trip home and the reload stay under the limited-ammo resource, as the registry's Generals ammunition note asks.

on_death.notes: From Veteran rank up, a Pilot gets out when it is destroyed: by parachute if it is shot down in flight, or beside the wreck if it dies on the ground, and he can take that rank into another USA vehicle (1.04 Object file; CNCNZ's Pilot entry; the registry's Generals pilots note). A plane without a rank leaves nobody behind. The Advanced Training upgrade at the Strategy Center, bought once for the whole side, doubles how fast it earns ranks (wiki, CNCNZ). Its crash effects in the 1.04 file are for show only.

strengths.why: On its supersonic attack run enemy fire cannot touch it (build tooltip, manual, CNCNZ), so anti-air defences cannot stop the bomb from landing; only a wide blast bursting right beside it can catch it (wiki).

Its build tooltip rates it strong against buildings: two Auroras together destroy most buildings, Auroras can pick off isolated base defences, and several can be thrown at a superweapon that is about to fire (wiki).
Its one bomb is among the deadliest single weapons in the game and, being no missile, cannot be jammed or shot down, so missile jammers and point-defence lasers are no help against it (wiki).
The blast covers a wide area, wrecking a cluster of stopped vehicles or a slow Overlord in one strike (wiki).
Even cruising it is about as fast as the Raptor, so it reaches distant targets in moments and suits quick follow-up strikes on a base whose power is down and whose defences are offline (wiki).

weaknesses.why: It carries a single bomb, then must fly back to an Air Field pad to reload it, so each strike is followed by a long round trip; it also needs a free pad to be built at all (wiki; registry ammunition note).

Once the bomb is away it slows at once and flies home slower than it cruises; with thin armour and half a Raptor's health it then falls fast to any anti-air or fighter that catches it (manual, tooltip, wiki), and ground fire can reach Auroras flying in a large group (manual).
The bomb falls on the point it was aimed at and does not track, so a vehicle that keeps moving can escape the blast (wiki), and a dropped bomb can never hit aircraft.
It depends on its Air Field: it is defenceless while parked there and needs a free pad to land and rearm (wiki).
No unit in the game costs more, so losing one is a crippling blow (wiki).

countered_by.why: Its build tooltip names anti-air units as a weakness, and after the release every kind of anti-air weapon can hit it; the wiki warns that laser and massed gunfire anti-air often kill it as it turns away from its target.
Its build tooltip also names fighters: enemy fighter jets can catch it on its slow flight home (manual, wiki).

counters.why: Buildings, by its build tooltip's strong line: two Auroras destroy most of them, Auroras pick off isolated base defences, and several can kill a superweapon about to fire, or fewer with help from a General's Power (wiki).
Vehicles that have stopped or bunched together, and slow ones: the wide blast wrecks them, though it misses a vehicle that keeps moving (wiki).
The same reason: the wiki names the slow Overlord as a fitting target.

combos.why: Best in numbers: two together destroy most buildings, and a superweapon about to fire takes several of them (wiki).
Its tooltip names fighters as its weakness, so friendly fighters or other anti-air covering its slow way home keep it alive to strike again (reasoned; see uncertain).

units.memorable: A supersonic jet that no gun can touch on its bombing run: one huge bomb nothing can jam or shoot down, then a slow, exposed flight home to rearm.
units.as_player: A T3 strike bomber with one big bomb per sortie. Left mouse picks a target: you go supersonic and untouchable for the run, release the bomb well short of it, then crawl home to rearm on a pad while fighters and anti-air hunt you. No other keys; aim at buildings and parked or slow vehicles, since the bomb follows nothing that moves.

sources.title: Command & Conquer: Generals - Zero Hour - USA Units, CNCNZ
sources.note: A long-standing fan site's unit list, cited as the second site, as the sources rule and the registry's CNCNZ note ask. Its Aurora entry agrees on the price, the Strategy Center, immunity to anti-aircraft fire on supersonic attack runs and a slower, subsonic flight home; its upgrades are Countermeasures (flares that help it evade missiles) and Advanced Training. Its Pilot entry has a pilot escape from a destroyed USA vehicle or aircraft with some experience and carry it into another vehicle. Fetched and read 2026-10-28.

uncertain.note: The base-game manual's Purpose entry for the Aurora Bomber reads Base Assault, which the registry lists among the entries that name no role, so step 1 goes on, and step 3 gives siege because the main weapon is a bomb dropped from the air. The Air Force General's build button shares the main tooltip; the Laser General's points at the Microwave Tank's tooltip, a slip in the 1.04 files (CommandButton.ini, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/CommandButton.ini, read, not cited), which the registry reads as neither carrying nor lacking the Aurora's lines.

Anti-infantry ranks at roles.secondary step 3 only because the bomb's blast covers an area, which makes it a splash weapon; no official text names soldiers among its targets, and the wiki aims it at buildings and vehicles. Raider ranks at step 4 (very fast, light armour) and fits loosely: it makes one bombing run and flies home rather than harassing. The tooltip's weak line names fighters and anti-air units, which would drop anti-air, a role it could not claim anyway.

Long by its reach, three times the Ranger rifle's in the wiki infobox and in Weapon.ini of the 1.04 files (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Weapon.ini, read, not cited), although bombs default to short. A comment there says the reach is set high because the plane moves so fast: the bomb is let go well before the target and flies on, and the bomb object in WeaponObjects.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/WeaponObjects.ini, read, not cited) has a fast locomotor of its own and does not follow its target. The reach stays well inside its fog-clearing sight, so it is not off-screen.

The wiki infobox and Weapon.ini (address under armament/0/range) give one blast with a modest radius, while the wiki's changelog says Zero Hour patch 1.03 raised the bomb's damage and radius to far larger figures. The old figures match the second blast of the Aurora Alpha's fuel-air bomb on its own wiki page (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Aurora_Alpha, read, not cited) and the new ones the unused fuel-air detonation weapon in the Air Force General's file (Object/AirforceGeneral.ini, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/AirforceGeneral.ini, read, not cited), so the changelog may describe the fuel-air bombs. The wiki's prose also calls the Aurora's bomb fuel-air, where its infobox lists a single conventional bomb. The splash trait and the explosive damage hold either way.

No friendly-fire: only Weapon.ini (address under armament/0/range) lets the blast hurt allies, and the registry's Generals note says a term that only those files would set is not set. No homing: the wiki says the bomb will not follow a target on the move, and its bomb object (address under armament/0/range) does not follow its target.

Three official unit descriptions in the cited string table list the Aurora beside the Stealth Fighter as a plane that Bunker Busters upgrade. The wiki's Bunker Busters page (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Bunker_Busters, read, not cited) gives it to the Stealth Fighter only and says the Aurora's upgrade voice lines are leftovers of an earlier plan, and the Aurora's 1.04 object has no upgraded weapon set. Left off.

become-invulnerable: for the run enemy fire cannot touch it, paid for by a slow, exposed trip home, and the counterplay is to let the bomb fall and strike the plane afterwards, as the pattern's summary has it. The immunity is not complete: the cited Object file makes attackers aim behind it and miss for a couple of seconds after each attack rather than ignoring damage, so a wide blast bursting beside it still hurts it (wiki), and the manual says ground fire can reach a large group. overclock-self was weighed for the speed burst and the slump afterwards, but the speeds alone are numbers, and the sources describe the immunity as the state; the slump is in the summary. See fit_notes.

The build tooltip says its speed falls to half after the attack. The wiki infobox's sluggish speed, which matches Locomotor.ini of the 1.04 files (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Locomotor.ini, read, not cited), is only a little below its cruise, and the wiki's changelog says Generals patch 1.03 raised the after-bomb speed from half its cruise, so the tooltip seems to describe the game before that patch; the changelog's raised figure is in turn lower than the infobox's. No band depends on it.

The comparisons with the Raptor, Stealth Fighter, Comanche and Chinook use their locomotors in Locomotor.ini (address under abilities/0/summary), read, not cited; the badly damaged speed comes from the wiki infobox.

The health comparisons and the set's values rest on the cited AmericaAir.ini and on AmericaInfantry.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/AmericaInfantry.ini) and Armor.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Armor.ini) of the 1.04 files, read, not cited. The wiki gives the Countermeasures flares a half chance to negate a missile attack, while the cited Object file's flare module diverts a smaller share of the missiles; CNCNZ says only that the flares help it evade missiles. The upgrade is side-wide either way.

The generals' versions rest on uncited 1.04 files: Object/AirforceGeneral.ini (address under armament/0) gives Granger's Aurora the plain Aurora Bomber name, the standard bomb, a lower price, half again the health and a point-defence laser; Object/LaserGeneral.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/LaserGeneral.ini) matches the main object; Object/SuperWeaponGeneral.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/SuperWeaponGeneral.ini) holds Alexander's Aurora Alpha Bomber with a fuel-air bomb weapon, the only Aurora his Air Field builds in CommandSet.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/CommandSet.ini). The string table's Fuel-Air Aurora Bomber name, under a label for Granger's object, is used by none of them. The wiki's Aurora Alpha page (address under armament/0) has the Alpha slow only in turns and fly home supersonic, while its 1.04 object keeps the Aurora's sluggish return; that point belongs to the Alpha's own entry.
Fighters: the tooltip's weak line names them, and fighters are jets, which fly in the high-air layer, so the entry names that layer rather than all aircraft.
Reasoned, not sourced as a pairing: it rests on the tooltip naming fighters as a weakness and on the manual and wiki saying it is exposed on its slow way home.

That the crash is only for show: the cited Object file's death modules call a list in ObjectCreationList.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/ObjectCreationList.ini, read, not cited) that throws out a hulk and nothing else, and no page says the crash hurts anything nearby, so no death blast. The pilot's parachute and ground lists are in the same file.

fit_notes.note: The registry's summary makes the user immune to damage for a moment at a cost. The Aurora's immunity comes with every attack order rather than a chosen moment, works by making aimed shots miss, and is paid for by a slow trip home rather than a cooldown.

units.name: Sentry Drone

tier.basis: Built at the USA War Factory with nothing else needed: its 1.04 Object file lists only that building, and the wiki infobox gives tier 1; the War Factory is basic production, t1 in the tier map. A Zero Hour addition (wiki; the Zero Hour manual lists it among the new USA units). Every USA side fields it from its own War Factory, with the gun upgrade sold there too (1.04 command sets): the Laser General's copy matches the main one, while the Air Force General's costs a little more and the Superweapon General's a quarter more, with the same body and modules (see cost_band). It has no button of its own beyond the basic orders.

cost_band.basis: Its list price, the same in the wiki infobox, on CNCNZ and as the build cost in its 1.04 Object file, is a little above the medium threshold and about the mean price of the three anchor tanks. Granger's version costs a little more and Alexander's a quarter more; both stay medium (wiki, 1.04 files). The gun and armour upgrades, each bought once for every drone, are left out.

mobility.notes: Its land speed in the wiki infobox and its 1.04 locomotor is three times the Ranger's, so very fast: the same as the Humvee's and twice the Crusader's, the USA main battle tank, and the wiki stresses how quick it is. It runs on treads (its 1.04 object leaves track debris, and the wiki compares it to an enlarged TALON robot), so tracks, a mobility whose speed list stops at fast; the validator records the break as atypical. The wiki notes a short delay before it obeys move orders: like the Nuke Cannon and the Listening Outpost it unpacks before its gun can fire and packs up before it can move, about a second each way in the 1.04 file, while attack orders within its reach are carried out at once. Badly damaged it slows a little, a game-wide rule. It crushes nothing (wiki; crusher level zero in the 1.04 file). The tracks' default handling stands.

body.notes: A small tracked robot; the gun upgrade adds a machine gun in its nose (manual) on a small turret (1.04 file). Size small: in transports the game handles it like a soldier, taking one slot as an infantryman does (wiki; 1.04 file), though it cannot ride in a Humvee's infantry seats (wiki). An uncrewed machine of that size is a drone.

armour.notes: Step 1 decided, through the registry's exception for one-off sets: its own Sentry Drone Armor (wiki infobox; 1.04 Object file) maps by what the unit is, and a drone no bigger than a soldier is light. Its health is a quarter more than a Humvee's and about five eighths of a Crusader's (1.04 files). The set halves damage from small arms, gattling and vulcan guns, infantry missiles, flame and crushing, lets through under a third of jet missile damage, and takes nothing from poison, lasers, sniper fire, microwaves or crew-killing shots (1.04 Armor.ini). One health bar, and no self-healing, since it never ranks. Drone Armor (CNCNZ calls it Scout Armour), bought once at the Strategy Center for every USA drone, adds a quarter to its health and, since Zero Hour patch 1.03, reaches the Sentry Drone too; the wiki says it then matches a Scorpion tank's toughness.

sensors.notes: Its fog-clearing figure, the second sight figure in the wiki infobox and its 1.04 ShroudClearingRange, is a little under the Ranger's, so medium. Detector: it uncovers camouflaged enemy units near it (its tooltip's opening line, a hint and the official unit descriptions), mines and GLA demo traps included (a campaign line), out to a little under two thirds of its fog-clearing sight (the wiki's detection figure; DetectionRange in the 1.04 file); the wiki has it expose them for nearby allies, so the team sees them too. Its own hiding is the cloak passive (abilities/0), as the registry's Generals stealth note asks, not the stealth trait.

armament.name: Sentry Drone Gun
armament.condition: Added by the Sentry Drone Gun upgrade, bought once at the War Factory for every Sentry Drone, those already in the field included (wiki, CNCNZ, 1.04 files); a stock drone is unarmed.
armament.summary: A 20mm machine gun in the drone's nose, which the upgrade fits to every drone (manual; upgrade tooltip): rapid shots that reach half again as far as the Ranger's rifle. The Zero Hour manual aims it at infantry and small vehicles, and the build tooltip rates the drone strong against infantry and weak against tanks; the wiki says it tears through soldiers and thin-skinned vehicles but does little to medium or heavy armour, and it cannot fire at aircraft. Its damage name, Comanche Vulcan (wiki infobox), is kinetic by the damage map. It fires only after the drone has stopped and unpacked, and each burst shows the drone to the enemy (abilities/0); since Zero Hour patch 1.03 a hidden drone no longer opens fire by itself (wiki changelog). The wiki's own page for the upgrade calls it a 20mm autocannon (see uncertain).

crew.notes: No crew: the wiki calls it an autonomous robot in its background and a remotely controlled, unmanned machine in its game section, and no operator stands on the field, so solo rather than remote. One player is the drone.

abilities.name: Stealth while still
abilities.summary: Always on, with no button: while it neither moves nor fires, enemies can neither see nor target it (manual, official unit descriptions, wiki, CNCNZ). Moving or firing shows it, and it hides again a couple of seconds after it stops (1.04 file). An enemy detector close by uncovers it, and once it is found, idle enemies within their reach are sent after it (1.04 file). Since Zero Hour patch 1.03 an armed drone holds its fire while hidden until it is ordered to shoot, so it stays hidden (wiki changelog). Coded as one passive with the cloak pattern, as the registry's Generals stealth note asks.

on_death.notes: In the sources it is simply gone: it cannot rank, so no Pilot gets out (registry note; its 1.04 object has no pilot module), and nothing it leaves can be repaired or recrewed. Respawn is the default for an uncrewed machine.

strengths.why: Reveals camouflaged enemies close by for the whole team, mines and GLA demo traps included: its tooltip's opening line, a hint and the campaign briefing that introduces it all say so, and the wiki has it expose hidden units for nearby allies to kill.

Unseen whenever it stands still and holds its fire, so a parked drone can watch a road or a base edge for as long as needed and, once armed, ambush what passes (manual, official unit descriptions, wiki).

With no crew aboard it is immune to Jarmen Kell's crew-killing snipe, to Hijackers and to the Nuke Cannon's neutron shells and neutron mines, all of which empty or steal crewed vehicles (wiki); its armour set takes nothing from crew-kill damage (1.04 file).
Three times a Ranger's pace and as quick as a Humvee, so it can rush to a key spot and keep watch there (wiki).

Once the gun is bought, the build tooltip rates it strong against infantry and an official description says it troubles foot soldiers; the wiki calls armed drones fine counter-snipers that find, chase and kill snipers.

weaknesses.why: Fragile: its main defence is not being seen, and once its own movement or firing or an enemy detector gives it away it cannot take much punishment (wiki), while idle enemies close by are sent straight at it (1.04 file).

Its only weapon comes with an upgrade bought at the War Factory, so a stock drone cannot shoot at all; even armed, the tooltip names tanks as its weakness, an official description calls it no match for tanks, and the gun cannot fire at aircraft (wiki).
A machine that never gains veterancy (wiki; its 1.04 object cannot rank), so it never fires faster, gets tougher or heals itself as ranked units do, and leaves no Pilot behind.
As a scout it is let down by a short delay before it obeys move orders, which the wiki calls its biggest drawback and the reason the Humvee scouts better.

countered_by.why: An enemy detector close by, a unit or a base defence, takes away its hiding, and once seen it is a fragile machine that soon goes down (wiki; reasoned, see uncertain).
Tanks: the tooltip's weak line names them and an official description calls the drone no match for them; the wiki adds that even its gun does little to medium or heavy armour.
Its gun cannot fire at aircraft (wiki), so fliers can hunt it freely once it is seen.

counters.why: Hidden units: it uncovers camouflaged enemies near it (tooltip, hint), and once armed it can find, chase and kill hidden snipers quickly, which the wiki says makes it a fine counter-sniper.
Units whose trick is killing a vehicle's crew or stealing the vehicle get nothing from it: Jarmen Kell's snipe, Hijackers and the Nuke Cannon's neutron shells (wiki).
Named by the wiki: neither his snipe nor his rifle can hurt it, it uncovers his camouflage, and once armed it can run him down.
Once armed, its build tooltip rates it strong against infantry, and an official description says it causes foot soldiers trouble.
Armed and hidden, it can slip in among enemy resource gatherers and shred the thin-skinned Chinese and GLA ones (wiki); it cannot touch the flying Chinooks of the USA.
A few armed drones lying in wait can destroy a group of thin-skinned artillery units before their guards get back (wiki).

combos.why: It takes only one soldier's room in the transport slots of aircraft, so an air transport can carry it to where it is needed, though it cannot ride in a Humvee (wiki).

units.memorable: A small robot on treads that vanishes whenever it parks, uncovers hidden snipers and mines for its team, and shrugs off crew snipes and hijackers because nobody is inside.
units.as_player: A cheap T1 scout on treads: very fast, invisible whenever you stop and hold fire, and it reveals cloaked enemies, mines and traps near you for the whole team. You spawn unarmed; once the gun upgrade is bought, left mouse fires a nose machine gun that shreds infantry and light vehicles, but you must stop to fire and firing gives you away. No other keys; tanks and aircraft are your enemies, while crew snipes and hijacks do nothing to you.

sources.note: A long-standing fan site's unit list, cited as the second site, as the sources rule and the registry's CNCNZ note ask. Its Sentry Drone entry agrees on the price and on a stealthed, unmanned vehicle meant for scouting and for finding stealthed units, whose upgrade adds a 20mm nose gun used on infantry and lighter vehicles. It gives the gun upgrade a lower price than the wiki (see uncertain) and calls the armour upgrade Scout Armour. Fetched and read 2026-10-28.

uncertain.note: The Zero Hour unit has no Purpose entry, and its build tooltip's opening line, that it detects stealth, names no role (registry). Step 2 applies because the stock drone is unarmed (its gun comes only with an upgrade), and its main action, watching unseen and uncovering hidden enemies, gives scout, whose requires it meets three ways: very fast, the cloak passive's stealth category and the detector trait. Official text points the same way: the Zero Hour manual's tactics name it as a cheaper recon option, and a campaign line has it spotting stealthed units.

Raider ranks at step 4 (very fast, light armour); its coding rule's need for a weapon that harms is met only by the upgrade gun. Anti-infantry ranks at step 5 from that gun (the tooltip's strong line names infantry, and it is a machine gun that does little to tanks). An official description calls the gun anti-personnel, an alias of anti-infantry, but it names the upgrade gun, not the unit, so it is not read as step 1; read that way, anti-infantry would come first. The tooltip's weak line names tanks, which drops anti-armour.

Machine gun, as the Zero Hour manual, the upgrade tooltip and the official unit descriptions call it, and as the wiki's own infobox and CNCNZ do. The wiki's Sentry drone gun page (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Sentry_drone_gun, read, not cited) calls it a 20mm autocannon, and the Sentry drone page's trivia calls it an auto cannon. The registry leaves its damage name to what the sources say the gun fires, and official text settles on a machine gun.

Hitscan is the machine-gun family's default, since no cited page says how the shots travel. Weapon.ini of the 1.04 files (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Weapon.ini, read, not cited) gives the gun no projectile object but a travel speed, a fact only those files give, so the registry's note leaves it unset. The same file confirms its Comanche Vulcan damage name and that it hits one target at a time.

Where the gun is bought: the wiki, CNCNZ and the 1.04 command sets (CommandSet.ini, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/CommandSet.ini, read, not cited) put it at the War Factory, while an in-game hint and an official unit description in the cited string table say the Strategy Center; the Strategy Center sets in CommandSet.ini still hold the button, commented out, so those lines seem to predate a move. CNCNZ also gives the upgrade a lower price than the wiki, whose figure Upgrade.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Upgrade.ini, read, not cited) backs, and the wiki's gun page (address under armament/0/family) a shorter research time than Upgrade.ini. No term depends on either.

Can_target step 3: an official unit description labels the gun anti-personnel, which gives infantry; the manual (small vehicles), CNCNZ (lighter vehicles) and the wiki (light vehicles, gatherers, artillery) add ground vehicles; and the wiki infobox's ground attack line belongs to the gun, the drone's only weapon, which counts as saying it hits structures. The wiki says it cannot fire at aircraft.

Small because the game handles it like a soldier in a transport: one slot, as an infantryman takes (wiki; the cited Object file). The wiki adds that it does not fit the infantry-only seats of ground vehicles such as the Humvee, so the game does not treat it as infantry everywhere.
The wiki calls it purely autonomous in its background and remotely controlled in its game section; neither puts an operator on the field, so the remote model's rule does not apply either way.

The delay on move orders: the wiki's trivia says the unpack step delays the drone by a few seconds on a move order, while the cited Object file sets about a second to pack and another to unpack. The comparison with the Humvee and the Crusader uses their locomotors in Locomotor.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Locomotor.ini, read, not cited), which also gives the drone's own locomotor a tread appearance.

The set's values rest on Armor.ini of the 1.04 files (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Armor.ini, read, not cited), the health comparisons on the cited Object file; Upgrade.ini (address under armament/0/condition) names the armour upgrade Drone Armor, as the wiki does.

The wiki names Kell's snipe, Hijackers, neutron shells and neutron mines; that the drone's set takes nothing from crew-kill damage is in Armor.ini (address under armour/notes). How the neutron shells and mines spare it was not traced in the files.

Reasoned from the wiki's counters section, which says its main defence is not being seen and that once exposed it soon goes down, and from the registry's Generals stealth note, by which a detector nearby uncovers a hidden unit; the wiki's Stealth page (https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Stealth, read, not cited) lists the Generals detectors, base defences such as the Gattling Cannon, Stinger Site and Tunnel Network among them. No page names detectors as its counter in so many words.

Left out: official descriptions of China's ECM Tank in the cited string table say its jamming field disables all drones near it, but in the 1.04 files that field deals a damage type the Sentry Drone's set ignores (ChinaVehicle.ini, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/ChinaVehicle.ini, with Weapon.ini and Armor.ini, read, not cited); only the tank's aimed disabler stops it, as it stops any vehicle.

The Kell, gatherer and artillery entries rest on the cited Sentry drone page; the wiki's gun page (address under armament/0/family) adds that neither Black Lotus nor Kell can harm an armed drone hunting them.

The cited Object file's death list in ObjectCreationList.ini (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/ObjectCreationList.ini, read, not cited) leaves only a hulk and debris for show; no page says it can be repaired, recrewed or salvaged, or that its end hurts anything nearby.

fit_notes.wanted: an automatic deploy step: the unit stops and unpacks before its weapon can fire and packs up before it moves, with no button
fit_notes.note: deploy-anchor needs a key and a stronger stationary mode; the Sentry Drone's unpacking happens by itself on every attack and only delays its next move order, which the wiki counts as its biggest drawback.

atypical.note: A small tracked robot that the wiki infobox and its 1.04 locomotor give three times the Ranger's land speed, as fast as the Humvee on its wheels; our tracks type stops at fast, but its locomotor runs on treads, so tracks stays and the band follows the figure.

units.name: Combat Chinook

tier.basis: Built at the Air Force General's Supply Center once a War Factory stands: its 1.04 Object file lists the War Factory as its prerequisite, the Supply Center builds it beside the ordinary Chinook, and the manual, the wiki and CNCNZ say the same. Both are basic production buildings, which the tier map puts at t1, so no tech building or promotion is needed; the gate names the War Factory, the extra building it waits for. Only the Air Force General fields it.

cost_band.basis: Its list price, the same in the wiki infobox, on CNCNZ and in its 1.04 Object file, falls between the high and very-high thresholds, about half again the anchor tanks' mean price, so high. The same general's ordinary Chinook costs about a fifth less (Chinook page).

mobility.notes: The wiki infobox gives a flying speed seven and a half times the Ranger's land speed, so very fast; like most units it slows down badly when heavily hurt, a game-wide rule the band leaves out. Among Generals aircraft it outflies the Comanche and doubles the Helix, and only jets such as the Raptor are quicker (1.04 locomotors; see uncertain); the wiki calls it fast and agile. It lands only to take riders on or let them off, or to be repaired (wiki). Strafe is the default for hovering flight.

body.notes: A twin-rotor transport helicopter, the ordinary Chinook given side ports for its riders (manual, wiki): large, as the sizes list puts transport helicopters. No source gives its footprint.

armour.notes: Step 1 decided: its set is Chinook Armor (wiki infobox; 1.04 Object file), which the armour_map makes light. The set takes half damage from most weapons and a quarter from infantry missiles, poison and radiation, while snipers, microwaves and melee do nothing to it (1.04 Armor.ini); it has a little more health than the ordinary Chinook (Chinook page), and Zero Hour patch 1.03 stopped flash-bangs hurting Chinooks. Its point-defence laser, which every Air Force General aircraft carries (manual), fires by itself at incoming missiles, several times a second and over a short reach; the wiki says it can stop a great many anti-air missiles, but bullets, shells and EMP pass it by, so it is the interceptor model. Countermeasures, an Air Field upgrade that gives flares to every USA aircraft (CNCNZ), is side-wide and left off. It never ranks up, so the self-healing of the top ranks never reaches it.

sensors.notes: Its fog-clearing figure, the second sight figure in the wiki infobox, is exactly one and a half times the Ranger's, which still counts as medium, as the registry's sight note says for the Chinook. Its first figure, how far it picks targets, is half that. Riders inside see nothing (game-wide), and a Pathfinder's stealth detection does not work from inside it (wiki). No sensor traits.

crew.notes: No player seats in the source, so solo is our proposal: the buyer flies it. Eight transport slots, copied from the source: a soldier fills one, a vehicle three and a construction dozer five (Chinook page; CNCNZ gives one and three), and aircraft cannot board. Soldiers fire their own weapons from the side ports, even in flight (manual, in-game hint), so passenger-firing; vehicles ride as cargo, though soldiers inside a carried Humvee fire from the ports too (wiki). Only Rangers can rope down in a Combat Drop (abilities/1). It lands to take riders on or let them off.

abilities.name: Gun ports (passenger seats)
abilities.summary: Up to eight soldiers, or fewer when vehicles take up room, ride inside; the soldiers shoot their own weapons out of the side ports even while it flies, so its firepower is whatever its riders bring, and empty it cannot attack. The manual and CNCNZ have the riders firing at ground targets. Everyone aboard dies if it is shot down (Chinook page). Loading, unloading and its Evacuate button are universal keys and stay off; it lands to unload.

abilities.name: Combat Drop
abilities.summary: Pointed at a building or a spot on the ground, the helicopter flies over it and hovers while its Rangers slide down four ropes, one after another, without it landing; other riders stay aboard, and it drops any supplies it holds. Into an empty building the Rangers garrison it. Into one held by enemy soldiers they kill the troops inside and then hold it themselves: the build tooltip and CNCNZ say the whole garrison is cleared, while the wiki has it cost one Ranger for each soldier inside (see uncertain). It needs at least one Ranger aboard and has no wait between uses (CNCNZ).

abilities.name: Supply runs
abilities.summary: Flown empty to a supply dock, it lowers a cargo net without landing, lifts a load of supply boxes and flies them to a Supply Center, where they become team money; it carries more per trip than any other gatherer, and the manual calls the Chinook the quickest and best of them. Only one Chinook works a dock at a time. It cannot collect while carrying anyone, and troops boarding make it drop the load it holds, which is lost (Chinook page). Supply Lines, bought at the Strategy Center, makes each load worth a little more (CNCNZ, wiki).

on_death.notes: In the source it spirals down, crashes and is simply gone; every rider dies with it, since its 1.04 Object file makes them lose all their health (the Chinook page agrees). It cannot rank up, so no Pilot ever ejects from it (Chinook page). So the 3C proposal applies: bail-out.

strengths.why: Soldiers inside fire from its side ports even in flight (in-game hint, manual); the wiki says a load of Missile Defenders and a Pathfinder makes it dangerous to almost any kind of unit.
Its point-defence laser shoots incoming missiles down by itself, and the wiki says it can stop a great many anti-air missiles (manual, wiki).
Fast and nimble: it outflies the Comanche, and the wiki praises it for quick raids that strike and pull back.
Flown empty it hauls the largest supply load of any gatherer, straight over the terrain and without landing, so far-off or contaminated docks are no trouble (Chinook page, manual).
Combat Drop ropes its Rangers into a building without landing, clearing out an enemy garrison and taking the building over (build tooltip, CNCNZ).

weaknesses.why: With no soldiers aboard it cannot attack, and arming it well is costly and needs careful handling near anti-air (wiki).
Everyone aboard dies when it is shot down (Chinook page), so a full load is a lot to lose.
It cannot collect while carrying anyone, and troops boarding make it drop a load it was holding, which is lost (Chinook page).
It has to land to load or unload troops, and while landed any ground unit can hit it (Chinook page, CNCNZ).
The laser only stops missiles: massed bullets and EMP get straight through, and the wiki calls it wide open to anti-air that does not fire missiles.
It never ranks up (Chinook page), so it never gains the extra health and self-healing that ranks bring.

countered_by.why: Gun-armed anti-air in numbers, the GLA Quad Cannon and the Chinese Gattling tank and Gattling Cannon, shoots it down, since its laser stops only missiles (wiki).
EMP weapons such as the EMP Patriot are a grave threat: one blast close by brings it down (wiki).
Anti-air units in groups take it down easily, Avengers above all (wiki).
The same reason: the wiki singles out the Avenger.

counters.why: Its laser shoots down incoming missiles by itself, so missile-firing anti-air (Patriots, Stinger Sites, missile infantry) and missile-armed fighters struggle against it; the wiki says it is weapons other than missiles that bring it down.

combos.why: Combat Drop works only with Rangers aboard: they rope down into a building and clear out the enemy soldiers holding it (build tooltip, CNCNZ, Chinook page); no other soldier can do it, so no word-list link covers the pairing.
Missile Defenders massed in its ports devastate vehicles and buildings (wiki).
The same reason: the wiki names the Missile Defender.
One Pathfinder aboard is enough against infantry (wiki), though his stealth detection does not work from inside.
The same reason: the wiki names the Pathfinder.
A Humvee carried inside lets its own riders fire from the Chinook's ports as well, so up to twelve soldiers can fight from one helicopter (wiki).
The same reason: the wiki names the Humvee.

units.memorable: The Air Force General's armed Chinook: soldiers shoot from its ports in flight, a laser knocks missiles out of the air, and Rangers rope down from it into enemy-held buildings.
units.as_player: A fast T1 transport helicopter with eight seats: teammates on foot fire their own weapons from its side ports even in flight, while you fly and a point-defence laser shoots down missiles aimed at you; alone you have no gun. Q (Combat Drop) ropes Ranger teammates down into a building, clearing out the enemy soldiers holding it, or onto open ground. Flown empty you can haul supplies for team money; gun-armed anti-air and EMP are what bring you down.

uncertain.note: Step 1 reads the opening line of its build tooltip, which names transport ('Assault Transport') and logistics ('Collects supplies'), as the registry note says; neither role has a target, so step 1 goes on. Step 2 applies because it has no weapon of its own, and transport is taken as its main action: the tooltip names it first, the Air Force General also fields the cheaper ordinary Chinook for supplies, and the manual and the wiki present the gun ports as what sets this one apart. Logistics would win if supply runs were read as its main action.

Logistics ranks at step 1 (the tooltip's supply line). Anti-infantry ranks at step 2: Combat Drop, a button every copy has, harms only the soldiers inside a building. The tie-break between the anti roles and engineer asks what it does once in: it kills the soldiers (anti-infantry) and then holds the building (engineer), and the tooltip's stated aim is the killing; anti-infantry also comes first in the roles list. Riders would add anti-armour and anti-air only at step 5. Raider fits the wiki's praise of it for raids, but those are the wiki's own words, and raider needs a weapon of the unit's own.

The 1.04 Object file named across this entry is Object/AirforceGeneral.ini of the unedited 1.04 files (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheSuperHackers/GeneralsGamePatch/6c7f40d6af6a4babb77a33a4502ec7656446c13e/Patch104pZH/GameFilesOriginalZH/Data/INI/Object/AirforceGeneral.ini, read, not cited), object AirF_AmericaVehicleChinook: display name, the War Factory as prerequisite, price, build time, both sight figures, never trainable, Chinook Armor, health, the Chinook supply module with its four ropes, eight transport slots that take infantry and vehicles but not aircraft or the largest vehicles, riders allowed to fire and losing all their health when it dies, a helicopter death spiral and the point-defence laser. The Combat Chinook page itself says only that the drop also works on enemy-held buildings. The four ropes come from the cited wiki pages.

drop-in-from-above, a planned pattern, for riders arriving on a chosen spot from a carrier that hovers over it. carry-passengers' hot-drop variant fits the rope drop too, but the passenger seats already link passenger-sets-weapon and Paired entries keeps the two patterns apart. capture-structure's take-over variant was weighed for clearing an enemy-held building, but the building is a civilian one the enemy only occupies, garrisoning is game-wide, and taking a neutral building is not that pattern (see fit_notes).

The 1.04 Object file (address under tier) gives it the same supply-gathering module as the ordinary Chinook, with eight boxes a load and a bonus behind Supply Lines, and ChinookAIUpdate.cpp (address under abilities/1) keeps it off supply runs while anyone is aboard. Counters holds only what it foils by itself, since it harms no enemy with a weapon or ability of its own (Matchups rule 5); its riders' and Rangers' work sits in combos. Missile anti-air, foiled by the laser alone, is in counters, while gun-armed anti-air and anti-air in groups, Avengers above all, are in countered_by: different enemies and situations.

The base unit is the ordinary USA Chinook, which the wiki's infobox names as its base unit; its id, like the ids of the Rangers, Missile Defenders, Pathfinders, Humvees and Avengers linked here, is the one its entry would get.
